confirmed.title: The lock schedule domain never resolves for any real device: lock week profiles are typed SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE and read back as domain="switch"
confirmed.claim: detectScheduleDomain resolves the domain from the schedule channel's type via domainFromWeekProfileType. That function maps a channel type to "lock" only for the prefixes LOCK_WEEK / DOOR_LOCK_WEEK (schedules.go:518). No such channel type exists: the only two lock devices in the embedded fleet, HmIP-DLD and HmIP-DLP, carry their week profile on a channel of type SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE, which is matched two cases earlier (schedules.go:511 `HasPrefix(channelType, "SWITCH_WEEK")`) and returns "switch". The device-actor fallback (domainFromActorType, which does know DOOR_LOCK) is unreachable because the WEEK_PROFILE branch already returned. Consequence: parseSimpleScheduleWithDomain's `if domain != "lock" { return entries }` (schedules.go:653) short-circuits, so lock_mode / lock_action / permission are never derived on read, and serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain (schedules.go:799) never applies applyLockEncoding on write. The whole lock-schedule surface — schedule.LockActionTable, DetectLockAction, lockPermissionDurationBase/Factor, simpleScheduleUnsupportedFields["lock"], and the SPA's lock mode/action pickers — is dead on every device it exists for.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Operator opens the week schedule of an HmIP-DLD (channel 10, SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE). GET /api/v1/devices/<addr>/schedule returns domain="switch" and no lock_mode/lock_action/permission on any entry, so the SPA renders an on/off Switch instead of the door-lock action picker. Toggling that switch and saving writes LEVEL=1.0 with no DURATION_BASE/DURATION_FACTOR keys at all (Duration is "" so BuildSimpleRawParamset emits nothing for it, rawconvert.go:787), leaving the slot's stored duration pair untouched. A slot that was `lock_autorelock_start` (level 0.0, base 0, factor 0) becomes (1.0, 0, 0) — a combination absent from schedule.LockActionTable — so the door lock now performs an action the operator never chose and which the daemon cannot even name on the next read.
confirmed.evidence: internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:509-526 domainFromWeekProfileType: `case strings.HasPrefix(channelType, "SWITCH_WEEK"): return "switch"` (:511) precedes `case strings.HasPrefix(channelType, "LOCK_WEEK"), strings.HasPrefix(channelType, "DOOR_LOCK_WEEK"): return "lock"` (:518). internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:486-495 returns on the first non-empty result for the schedule channel, so the domainFromActorType fallback (:497-501, which maps DOOR_LOCK -> "lock" at :543) never runs. tests/integration/testdata/model_snapshot_openccu-loom.json: HmIP-DLD channels are 0 MAINTENANCE, 1 DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER, 2-9 ACCESS_RECEIVER, 10 SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE; HmIP-DLP channel 14 is SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE. Distinct *_WEEK_PROFILE channel types across all 399 devices: BLIND_, DIMMER_, DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR_, SHADING_, SWITCH_, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_, WATER_SWITCH_ — no LOCK_/DOOR_LOCK_/COVER_/SHUTTER_/VALVE_/LIGHT_ variant exists. Consumers verified dead: internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:650-675 (read) and :796-809 (write).
confirmed.verifier_reason: Code says what the evidence claims and the fleet backs it. detectScheduleDomain (schedules.go:481-503) returns on the first non-empty domainFromWeekProfileType for the schedule channel, so the domainFromActorType fallback (which does map DOOR_LOCK/KEYMATIC -> lock) is unreachable whenever the week-profile channel type already matches. Measured against the embedded godevccu fleet (399 device descriptions) with the production functions themselves: 45 models carry a *_WEEK_PROFILE channel; the only channel types present are BLIND_/DIMMER_/DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR_/SHADING_/SWITCH_/UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_/WATER_SWITCH_ — no LOCK_WEEK or DOOR_LOCK_WEEK anywhere — and 0 of 45 resolve to "lock". All three lock models with a week profile (HmIP-DLD ch10, HmIP-DLP ch14, HmIP-WKP ch18) resolve to "switch". Reachable: HmIP-DLD ch10 MASTER really carries 75 slots x {LEVEL, DURATION_BASE, DURATION_FACTOR, TARGET_CHANNELS, WEEKDAY, FIXED_HOUR, FIXED_MINUTE}, the WEEK_PROFILE-suffix channel passes deviceHasRegisteredScheduleChannel, so GET .../schedule returns kind=simple with domain="switch" and the SPA takes the `domain === "switch"` branch — a binary on/off Switch — instead of the `domain === "lock"` mode/action/permission pickers (SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:333-336 vs :378-465). No guard rescues it: stripUnsupportedFields("switch") drops only level_2 and ramp_time, so a pure read/save round-trip is lossless, but every lock-specific field (lock_mode / lock_action / permission) is nil on read and the lock decode branch (schedules.go:653) is never entered. Two corrections to the claimant: (a) the write-side lock encoding is NOT strictly dead — PutClimateSchedule passes sched.Domain from the *request body* (schedules.go:919), so an API client that PUTs domain:"lock" still gets applyLockEncoding; only the SPA (which sends no domain) and the read path are dead; (b) the corruption micro-detail is off — FormatTimeBaseFactor(0,0) returns ZeroDuration "0ms", not "", so DURATION_BASE/FACTOR are emitted as (0,0) rather than omitted. The end state the claimant predicts is unchanged: toggling the switch on a slot that was lock_autorelock_start yields the triplet (1.0, 0, 0), which is absent from schedule.LockActionTable, and level 1.01 ("open") silently degrades to 1.0 ("unlock") on any toggle. Severity kept at high: the feature is 100% unreachable on 100% of the devices it exists for, on a security-relevant device class, and an operator edit through the wrong widget writes an unlock action. Not fixed on origin/main (d281e2e2 == local HEAD). Existing tests are textbook bracketing: schedules_pure_test.go:187/194 asserts domainFromWeekProfileType("LOCK_WEEK_PROFILE"/"DOOR_LOCK_WEEK_PROFILE") == "lock" for channel types that exist in no device, and every other lock test passes the literal "lock" straight into parse/serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain.
confirmed.verifier_evidence: internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:481-503 (return on first non-empty), :509-526 (domainFromWeekProfileType), :650-675 (`if domain != "lock" { return entries }`), :919 (write domain comes from the request DTO). Fleet sweep with the production functions over $GOMODCACHE/github.com/!sukram!j/godevccu@v0.2.2/internal/embed/data/device_descriptions/*.json (temp test, deleted): 45 week-profile models -> switch 26, light 8, cover 5, valve 1, "" 5, lock 0; HmIP-DLD:10 / HmIP-DLP:14 / HmIP-WKP:18 all TYPE=SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE. paramset_descriptions/HmIP-DLD.json VCU9724704:10 MASTER = 525 keys, slots 01..75, fields {DURATION_BASE, DURATION_FACTOR, FIXED_HOUR, FIXED_MINUTE, LEVEL, TARGET_CHANNELS, WEEKDAY}. assets/ui/src/lib/components/schedule/SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:333 `{#if domain === "switch"}` -> `<Switch checked={entry.level >= 0.5} onCheckedChange={(v) => patch(idx, { level: v ? 1 : 0 })} />`; :378 `{:else if domain === "lock"}` unreachable. internal/model/schedule/lock.go:29-34 LockActionTable {autorelock_start (0.0,0,0), autorelock_end (0.0,7,31), unlock (1.0,7,31), open (1.01,7,31)}. internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:994 `const ZeroDuration = "0ms"`, :786-793 duration emitted only when non-empty. internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:621-627 simpleScheduleUnsupportedFields["switch"] = {level_2, ramp_time} (duration survives). Bracketing tests: internal/central/adapter/schedules_pure_test.go:187,194.

confirmed.title: The SPA still caps simple schedules at 24 slots after the daemon-side cap was raised to 75 (half-applied fix 8cbd2e12)
confirmed.claim: Commit 8cbd2e12 ("week-profile groups past 24") replaced the hard-coded 24 with schedule.SimpleMaxSlot = 75 in six Go call sites (internal/model/schedule/simple.go:329, internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:58, internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:748, pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:298 all now say 75/1..75). Its diff touched no SPA file. nextFreeSlot() in the only simple-schedule editor still searches slots 1..24 only and returns -1 beyond that, and the i18n catalogues hard-code "/ 24 slots" and "Maximum of 24 entries reached." in both locales.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An HmIP-PSM (SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE, 75 declared groups) already carries 24 switching points, configured either in the CCU WebUI or over REST. The operator opens the schedule editor and presses "Add slot": every slot in 1..24 is taken, nextFreeSlot() returns -1, and the operator gets the toast "Maximum of 24 entries reached." — although the daemon, the REST DTO and the device all accept slot 25..75. The header additionally reads "25 / 24 slots" for a schedule the CCU already holds.
confirmed.evidence: assets/ui/src/lib/components/schedule/SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:88-92 `function nextFreeSlot(): number { const used = new Set(entries.map((e) => e.slot_no)); for (let i = 1; i <= 24; i++) if (!used.has(i)) return i; return -1; }`; :106-113 addEntry() toasts t("schedule.max_reached") on -1. assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:2637 `"schedule.slots_count": "{count} / 24 slots"`, :2640 `"schedule.max_reached": "Maximum of 24 entries reached."`, :6753/:6757 the German twins. Daemon side: internal/model/schedule/simple.go:329 `const SimpleMaxSlot = 75`; internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:58 `const SimpleMaxGroup = schedule.SimpleMaxSlot`; internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:748 rejects only `e.SlotNo < 1 || e.SlotNo > schedule.SimpleMaxSlot`.
confirmed.verifier_reason: Both numbers verified in current HEAD. SPA: SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:88-92 `for (let i = 1; i <= 24; i++) if (!used.has(i)) return i; return -1;` and addEntry() (:106-113) toasts t("schedule.max_reached") on -1; i18n.ts:2637/2640 (EN) and :6753/6757 (DE) hard-code "{count} / 24 slots" / "Maximum of 24 entries reached." and the German twins. confirmed.title: The CONFIG_PENDING reload hook refreshes only climate week profiles, so a non-climate schedule stays at its boot snapshot
confirmed.claim: wireConfigPendingHook reloads `wp.Climate()` for every channel of the settled device and skips channels whose Climate() is nil (auto_refresh.go:107-129). It never touches `wp.Simple()`. The only production call to Simple().Load is the one-shot background warm-up inside publishScheduleEntitySnapshot (eventbridge.go:2806-2815), which runs from publishCentralSnapshot — i.e. at boot, on southbound-ready, on a broker reconnect and on a config reload, never on a schedule change. ProfileDataPoint.ReloadSchedule, which would reload either kind, has no production caller at all. So the cached *schedule.Simple that feeds the MQTT Zeitplan surface is never re-read after the snapshot pass.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Operator edits the switching programme of an HmIP-PSM (SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE) — either in the OpenCCU-Loom SPA, which writes the MASTER paramset through the backend directly (PutClimateSchedule) and not through wp.Simple(), or in the CCU WebUI. The CCU fires CONFIG_PENDING; the settle hook finds Climate() == nil on that channel and does nothing. The retained MQTT attribute `schedule_data.entries` and the Zeitplan sensor's entry count keep the pre-edit slots until the daemon restarts or the broker reconnects. Home Assistant shows a schedule the device no longer runs.
confirmed.evidence: internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:108-129 — `wp := ch.WeekProfile(); if wp == nil { continue }; cp := wp.Climate(); if cp == nil { continue } ... cp.Load(ctx)`; no Simple() branch. internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2806-2815 is the sole `capturedSP.Load(loadCtx)`, reached from publishScheduleEntitySnapshot -> publishDeviceSnapshot -> publishCentralSnapshot (eventbridge.go:611-637), whose callers are PublishInitialSnapshot / the southbound-ready path / the broker-reconnect reseed (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:295,347; daemon_southbound.go:401). `grep -rn "ReloadSchedule" --include=*.go internal/ cmd/ | grep -v _test.go` yields only the definition at internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:942. The stale snapshot is what is published: eventbridge.go:3150 `attrs["schedule_data"] = map[string]any{"entries": simpleScheduleEntriesJSON(wp)}` and :3163-3166 `sp.Current()`.
confirmed.verifier_reason: The cited code says exactly what the evidence claims and I found no other refresh path. auto_refresh.go:108-129 loops the device's channels, takes `wp := ch.WeekProfile()`, then `cp := wp.Climate(); if cp == nil { continue }` and calls `cp.Load(ctx)` — `wp.Simple()` is never touched. I swept every candidate the brief asked for. (a) Event-driven reload: SetOnConfigSettled has exactly ONE consumer, this hook (coordinators/event.go:87 -> auto_refresh.go:89). (b) Periodic job: the scheduler registers firmware_check, health_heartbeat, check_connection, hub.*_refresh, refresh_client_data, reconcile and scheduled_backup — none reloads a week profile; no grep hit for weekprofile in internal/scheduler or the job files. (c) Cache invalidation on paramset write: PutClimateSchedule (schedules.go:955-982) calls backend.PutParamset and then only audit.Record — it never touches the ProfileDataPoint, so the write that causes the drift is also the write that cannot heal it. (d) The generic reload API is dead: `ReloadSchedule` (weekprofile/datapoint.go:942) has test callers only. (e) The Simple saver (week_profile_io.go:146-159) likewise has no production caller, so nothing else fires OnChange. That leaves eventbridge.go:2806-2815 as the sole production `sp.Load`, reached only from publishScheduleEntitySnapshot <- publishDeviceSnapshot <- publishCentralSnapshot / onDeviceCreated — i.e. boot, per-central southbound-ready, broker reconnect, and a genuinely new device. beginBackgroundLoad (eventbridge.go:242-250) has no budget cap, so those paths do re-load; "forever" is therefore an overstatement, but the claim itself enumerates the same exceptions and none of them is a schedule edit. Impact is confined to the MQTT plane: REST/SPA reads are live (GetClimateSchedule does a fresh backend.GetParamset), so the operator sees the new schedule in the SPA while the retained `schedule_data.entries` attribute and the Zeitplan sensor's entry count (eventbridge.go:3150, :3163-3166) keep the pre-edit slots. Read-only display drift, no control path affected — medium holds. Not fixed on origin/main.
confirmed.verifier_evidence: internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:108-129 `wp := ch.WeekProfile(); if wp == nil { continue }; cp := wp.Climate(); if cp == nil { continue } ... cp.Load(ctx)`. internal/central/coordinators/event.go:87 (sole SetOnConfigSettled seam) + auto_refresh.go:89 (sole consumer). internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:955-982 (PutParamset then audit only). internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:942 ReloadSchedule — callers only in datapoint_test.go:558/579/587. Production `sp.Load` grep: eventbridge.go:2813 and datapoint.go:957 (inside dead ReloadSchedule) only.

confirmed.title: MQTT hard-codes schedule_domain="switch" for every non-climate week profile — but no consumer anywhere reads the field
confirmed.claim: publishScheduleEntityPayload hard-codes `attrs["schedule_domain"] = "switch"` in the non-climate branch. The REST/WS surface derives the real bucket per device (SchedulesDomain.detectScheduleDomain, schedules.go:477-505) and returns switch / light / cover / valve / lock, so the two north-bound planes disagree for the majority of schedule devices.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An HmIP-BROLL (BLIND_WEEK_PROFILE) and an HmIP-RGBW (UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_WEEK_PROFILE) both publish `schedule_domain: "switch"` on their Zeitplan json_attributes topic while REST reports "cover" for the first. Any HA template or external client that branches on schedule_domain (the field exists for exactly that) renders an on/off switch editor for a blind and a colour-capable light, and would write binary levels to a device whose level is a 0..1 position.
confirmed.evidence: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:3130-3152 — the whole `else` (non-climate) branch ends with `attrs["schedule_domain"] = "switch"` with no reference to the device or its channel types. Contrast internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:446 `domain := s.detectScheduleDomain(deviceAddress, channelNo)` feeding hmapi.ClimateSchedule.Domain (:451). Affected models from tests/integration/testdata/model_snapshot_openccu-loom.json: BLIND_WEEK_PROFILE on HmIP-BROLL/FROLL/FBL/DRBLI4 and HmIPW-DRBL4, DIMMER_WEEK_PROFILE on HmIP-BDT/FDT/SCTH230/DRDI3/UDI-SMI55 and HmIPW-DRD3, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_WEEK_PROFILE on HmIP-RGBW/LSC/DRG-DALI, WATER_SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE on ELV-SH-WSM, SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE on HmIP-HDM1/HDM2 — 20 of the 45 models that carry WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS.
confirmed.verifier_reason: The hard-coding is verbatim and reachable: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:3151 `attrs["schedule_domain"] = "switch"` sits at the end of the non-climate else-branch of publishScheduleEntityPayload, which has three production callers (:2829, :2867, :2879) and no reference to the device or its channel types. The disagreement with REST is real and measured: running the production domain functions over the 45 week-profile-bearing models in the embedded fleet gives switch 26, light 8, cover 5, valve 1, empty 5 — so 19 of 45 models are published as "switch" while REST reports cover / light / valve / nothing (the claimant said 20; the one-model delta comes from the actor-scan fallback running in device-channel order). Locks are not among the disagreeing models because REST already calls them "switch" too (see C21-schedules-1). Severity re-rated down from medium to low because the impact chain does not close: `schedule_domain` occurs exactly twice in the whole repository — this hard-code and a doc comment in internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:339 — and appears nowhere in docs/ (the MQTT schedule attribute block is undocumented), nowhere in assets/openapi.yaml or assets/wsapi.json, nowhere in the SPA, and in no sibling repo's consumption of our MQTT plane (the only local consumers of a field by that name are the HA-side card and homematicip_local, which read aiohomematic's own WeekProfileDataPoint.schedule_domain over the HA WebSocket API, not our topics). So the observable consequence today is a wrong value on an undocumented attribute that no shipped client branches on. Worth noting for the fix: the model API that would carry the right value is itself dead — ProfileDataPoint.ScheduleDomain() (datapoint.go:342) has no production caller and its input, ProfileDataPointConfig.ScheduleCategory, is never populated outside tests, so the eventbridge would have to call the adapter-package detectScheduleDomain instead. Not fixed on origin/main.
confirmed.verifier_evidence: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:3091-3152 (signature takes *weekprofile.ProfileDataPoint; the else-branch ends with the hard-code), callers at :2829/:2867/:2879. Contrast internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:446-453 (REST derives the domain per device). Repo-wide grep for `schedule_domain` over *.go/*.svelte/*.ts/*.md/*.yaml/*.json (excluding node_modules, spa_dist): 2 hits total — eventbridge.go:3151 and internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:339. internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:342-351 ScheduleDomain() — grep shows the definition only, no caller; `ScheduleCategory` is set only at datapoint.go:223 from a config field nothing populates in production. Fleet sweep (temp test, deleted): 45 week-profile models -> 26 switch / 8 light / 5 cover / 1 valve / 5 empty / 0 lock.

confirmed.title: The MQTT schedule payload's lock_mode / lock_action / permission fields are structurally always null
confirmed.claim: simpleEntryJSON emits lock_mode, lock_action and permission from schedule.SimpleEntry.LockMode/LockAction/Permission. Nothing on any read path ever sets those three fields. The only producer of the *schedule.Simple that reaches this function is weekprofile.ParseSimpleRawParamset via defaultChannelLoader.Load, and it builds the entry without them; the lock derivation lives exclusively in the REST adapter and operates on the hmapi DTO, not on the domain type. The three keys are therefore published as JSON null on every device, forever.
confirmed.failure_scenario: HmIP-DLD's Zeitplan json_attributes topic carries `schedule_data.entries["1"] = {..., "lock_mode": null, "lock_action": null, "permission": null}`. An HA template or external consumer that reads lock_action to show which door-lock action a slot performs gets nothing, on every slot of every lock, while the fields' presence in the payload advertises that the information is there.
confirmed.evidence: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2959-2973 builds lockMode/lockAction/permission from `e.LockMode`/`e.LockAction`/`e.Permission` and emits them at :2970-2972. internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:660-686 constructs schedule.SimpleEntry with Weekdays/Time/Level/Level2/Condition/AstroOffsetMinutes/TargetChannels/AstroType/Duration/RampTime/Color*/OutputBehaviour only. internal/central/adapter/week_profile_io.go:117-131 is the sole loader behind wp.Simple(); its saver (:146-159) has no production caller, so nothing else can populate the cached value. `grep -rn "LockMode:\|LockAction:\|Permission:" --include=*.go internal/ | grep -v _test.go` shows the only writers are internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:665-671 on hmapi.SimpleScheduleEntry and internal/model/schedule/simple.go:309-310 in EmptySimpleEntry, which has no production caller.
confirmed.verifier_reason: Proved directly rather than by grep. A temporary in-package test fed a lock-encoded raw paramset (01_WP_LEVEL=1.0, DURATION_BASE=7, DURATION_FACTOR=31, TARGET_CHANNELS=1 -> "1_1") through the real production read path weekprofile.ParseSimpleRawParamset and then through simpleEntryJSON: the domain entry came back LockMode="" LockAction="" Permission="", and the emitted JSON carried lock_mode=<nil> lock_action=<nil> permission=<nil> while target_channels=[1_1] and level=1 arrived intact — the information is on the wire and is discarded. The writer sweep confirms why: the only assignments to schedule.SimpleEntry.LockMode/LockAction/Permission in non-test code are simple.go:309-310 inside EmptySimpleEntry, which has zero callers anywhere in the repo (definition only), and schedules.go:665-671, which writes hmapi.SimpleScheduleEntry — the REST DTO, a different type that never reaches the cached *schedule.Simple. rawconvert.go:660-686 constructs the entry without them, and defaultChannelLoader (week_profile_io.go:117-131) is the sole loader behind wp.Simple(), whose saver has no production caller. So the three keys are JSON null on every device, always. Severity re-rated medium->low on the consumer question. For every non-lock device — which is every device that reaches this payload in practice, see C21-schedules-2 — null IS the correct "not applicable", and the plane gives the consumer no reason to expect otherwise: publishScheduleEntityPayload hard-codes `attrs["schedule_domain"] = "switch"` (eventbridge.go:3151) for every non-climate schedule, so nothing in the payload advertises a lock. A consumer genuinely cannot tell null from not-applicable, but the only case where that distinction would carry information (a real HmIP-DLD/DLP) is also mislabelled schedule_domain=switch, so the defect is informational, on a read-only attribute, with no control path behind it. Not fixed on origin/main.
confirmed.verifier_evidence: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2959-2973 (lockMode/lockAction/permission built from e.LockMode/e.LockAction/e.Permission) and :3151 (`attrs["schedule_domain"] = "switch"` unconditionally). internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:660-686. internal/model/schedule/simple.go:300-313 EmptySimpleEntry — repo-wide grep finds no caller. internal/central/adapter/week_profile_io.go:117-131 / :146-159. Temp test output: `domain entry: LockMode="" LockAction="" Permission=""` / `json: lock_mode=<nil> lock_action=<nil> permission=<nil> target_channels=[1_1] level=1`.

confirmed.title: MCP write_paramset writes MASTER without the edit lock REST and WS require unconditionally (LINK is not reachable via MCP)
confirmed.claim: REST and WS both refuse a MASTER (and LINK) paramset write unless the caller holds the per-resource edit session and presents its token: internal/north/rest/handlers/paramsets.go:100-104 calls enforceEditLock(w, r, locks, "channel:"+addr+":"+key) and answers 423 Locked, and internal/north/rest/ws/commands_extended.go:717-721 mirrors it with CommandErrorLocked. The MCP tool calls the same domain object (both are d.paramsetsDomain, daemon_rest_mount.go:294 and :684) but goes straight to d.Paramsets.PutParamset with no lock check at all. It is the only north-bound MASTER-write path with no edit-lock gate, and neither the code comment (tools.go:497-508, which discusses only audit rows and provenance) nor docs/external-clients/mcp.md nor ADR 0025 declares the divergence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An operator opens a channel's configuration in the SPA, which takes the edit session for `channel:0001D3C99C1234:1:MASTER`; every other REST/WS client is now answered 423. An assistant with an operator token then calls write_paramset {central_name, address:"0001D3C99C1234:1", key:"MASTER", values:{...}}. The write reaches the CCU while the SPA session still believes it holds exclusive edit rights; when the operator saves their (now stale) buffer the assistant's change is silently reverted — exactly the concurrent-edit collision the lock exists to prevent.

confirmed.title: MQTT VALUES writes reach the CCU with no parameter.Coerce / parameter.Validate — REST's sibling path does both, and validate.go's doc comment falsely names the MQTT subscriber as a caller
confirmed.claim: REST's PutDataPointValue (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:806-819) explicitly calls parameter.Coerce(dp.ParameterData(), req.Value) and then ch.Set(...) with SetOptions{Validate:true}, with a comment explaining why: an integer-valued JSON number must be coerced to the descriptor's declared type before dispatch, otherwise the wire type is wrong. MQTTCommandSink.SetValue (the VALUES-paramset MQTT command path, wired from every HA MQTT switch/light/number/cover/climate/select command) instead resolves ch.Writer() and calls w.SetValue(ctx, channelAddress, parameter, value, priority) directly — the raw ChannelWriter, never Channel.Set, never parameter.Coerce, never parameter.Validate. The incoming `value` comes from command_subscriber.go's parseCommandPayload, a descriptor-unaware string→Go-type guesser (ParseInt, then ParseFloat, then json.Unmarshal) that has no idea whether the target parameter is FLOAT, INTEGER, ENUM or BOOL. The Go dynamic type it produces is what internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:goToXMLRPCValue uses to pick the XML-RPC wire tag (int64→<i4>, float64→<double>) — so the wrong Go type silently becomes the wrong wire type. MIN/MAX/VALUE_LIST bounds are likewise never checked on this path. The sibling MASTER-paramset MQTT command (MQTTCommandSink.SetMasterValue, line 203) does route through Channel.Set but constructs SetOptions{Optimistic:true, Priority:priority} without Validate:true, so validateForSet/ValidateWithDP never runs there either — the same gap via the other paramset. grep confirms parameter.Coerce/parameter.Validate/ValidateWithDP have zero occurrences anywhere under internal/north/mqtt or in mqtt_sink.go, and ValidateWithDP (internal/parameter/validate.go) has exactly one caller in the whole non-test codebase (internal/model/device/channel_set.go's validateForSet), which the MQTT path never reaches. The doc comment on ValidateWithDP (validate.go:85-86) claims 'REST PUT /value handlers, MQTT command subscriber, WS dp-write handlers' as its callers — the MQTT half of that claim is false.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Home Assistant MQTT number entity for a FLOAT parameter (e.g. a HmIP thermostat SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE) publishes the whole-number payload "21" to <central>/<iface>/<addr>/<ch>/values/SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE/set. parseCommandPayload("21") returns int64(21) (ParseInt succeeds before ParseFloat is tried). That int64 flows unmodified through MQTTCommandSink.SetValue → Channel.Writer().SetValue → xmlrpcCaller.callRaw → goToXMLRPCValue, which encodes it as an XML-RPC <i4> integer instead of <double> — the exact FLOAT-vs-int wire-type drift the REST comment at devices.go:800-805 was written to prevent. Separately, any MQTT publisher (malicious, misconfigured automation, or a stale HA config) can send a value outside the parameter's MIN/MAX or an index outside VALUE_LIST and it reaches the CCU with zero client-side rejection — unlike REST, which answers 400 via device.ErrValidation.

confirmed.title: REST/SPA sysvar rename strands the HA entity until the next daemon restart: old discovery config never retracted, new one never announced
confirmed.claim: Hub.RenameSysvar (called from UpdateSysvarRemote, which PatchSysvar hits on a non-empty new_name) re-keys the sysvar map and calls Sysvar.SetName in place, preserving the pointer. It fires neither Hub.OnSysvarRegistered observers (only PutSysvar does, and PutSysvar is never called on rename) nor Sysvar.NotifyRemoved. Sysvar.MQTTTopics(...) and sysvarSpecFor(...) derive both the discovery payload and the retained state/set topics from Sysvar.LegacyName() freshly on every publish (sysvar.go:667-682, hub_mqtt_publisher.go:675-698), and Bridge.PublishSysvar publishes retained=true to sv.MQTTTopics(...).State (bridge.go:1233-1245). Because wireOneSysvar subscribes once (at wiring time) to the one live Sysvar pointer and never re-subscribes or republishes discovery on rename, and because the periodic hub refresh's upsertSysvar (hub_wiring.go:1172-1226) finds the already-renamed object by its new name (ok=true) and therefore never calls PutSysvar (that only fires for ok=false, i.e. a genuinely new name) -- no code path ever republishes or retracts sysvar discovery after a rename.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Operator renames a sysvar from Urlaub to Ferien via PATCH /api/v1/sysvars/Urlaub with name=Ferien. UpdateSysvarRemote succeeds on the CCU, then calls h.RenameSysvar(Urlaub,Ferien), re-keying the same *Sysvar pointer. The next confirmed value change publishes retained state to the NEW topic base/central/hub/sysvars/Ferien/state (MQTTTopics reads LegacyName() fresh). Home Assistant's existing entity, however, was discovered under the OLD retained discovery config (built with name Urlaub at wiring time or the last discovery republish) and still points its state_topic at .../Urlaub/state. That old retained discovery message is never retracted (no NotifyRemoved fires), and no new discovery message for Ferien is ever published (PutSysvar never fires for the existing pointer). Result: the HA entity freezes at its last pre-rename value forever, while the daemon publishes live updates to a topic HA was never told about.

No test covers rename+MQTT republish: internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery_sysvar_names_test.go only covers name-escaping in a single BuildSysvarDiscovery call, and internal/north/mqtt/retain_cleanup_test.go's rename-related tests are about central-name-escaping spelling drift across builds, not sysvar rename.

RenameSysvar re-keys the map and calls SetName on the SAME pointer; it fires neither the OnSysvarRegistered observers (only PutSysvar does) nor NotifyRemoved. The periodic 30 s refresh (internal/central/jobs.go:631 hub.sysvar_refresh, defaultSysvarRefreshSlot=30s) then finds the entry under the NEW name, so upsertSysvar takes the ok=true branch and never calls PutSysvar, and pruneRemovedSysvars finds nothing stale to remove. The only other republish path, HubChannelsAssignedEvent -> republishHubEntityDiscovery, fires only when assignHubChannels actually CHANGES a device link (`if changed`), which a plain rename normally does not — and even then it publishes the new config without retracting the old one. confirmed.title: The single shared MQTT collector is named after cfg.Centrals[0] but counts every central's traffic - documented per-Unit separation does not exist
confirmed.claim: NewMqttCollector's doc comment states the central_name is embedded in the metric name so multi-CCU daemons keep counters separated per Unit (internal/metrics/mqtt_collector.go:22-24). In production, however, exactly one MqttCollector is ever constructed, for the single shared mqtt.Bridge that serves every central, and it is built with centralName = pickFirstCentral(cfg) -- literally cfg.Centrals[0].Name. Every publish through that one Bridge (regardless of which central's topic it targets) increments the SAME counter set (b.collector.MessagesSent.Inc(), DiscoverySent, PublishErrors -- bridge.go:1940-1954; ReceivedCommands/SubscribeFailures in command_subscriber.go:576-583), because Bridge/CommandSubscriber hold one collector reference, not one per central.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A daemon configured with two CCUs, central names HouseA and HouseB (HouseA listed first in config). Prometheus exposes only mqtt_HouseA_messages_sent (and its sibling counters) -- mqtt_HouseB_messages_sent is never registered. All of HouseB's MQTT publish traffic (state, discovery, publish errors) is silently counted into mqtt_HouseA_messages_sent instead. An operator dashboarding per-CCU MQTT throughput/error-rate for HouseB sees a metric that does not exist, and HouseA's own metric is inflated by HouseB's unrelated traffic -- directly contradicting the collector's own documented per-Unit-separation contract.

confirmed.verifier_reason: Construction verified: NewMqttCollector is called exactly once in production (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:172, the only non-test call site repo-wide) with pickFirstCentral(cfg) = cfg.Centrals[0].Name, and wired via the single mqttSupervisor.SetCollector (daemon_infra.go:179, only production call). The stack it feeds is daemon-global, not per-central: buildSwap builds ONE bridge from the whole cfg (mqtt_supervisor.go:550-556) and the one CommandSubscriber resolves all centrals via `.WithCentralNames(reg)` (mqtt_supervisor.go:764-767). All six increment sites are unconditional with no per-central selection (bridge.go:1937-1955 incMessagesSent/incDiscoverySent/incPublishErrors; command_subscriber.go:576,583; daemon_north.go:685-686). No guard, ADR or by_design entry exempts it. Two-CCU operator (HouseA first) sees exactly one family: mqtt_HouseA_messages_sent / _discovery_sent / _publish_errors / _received_commands / _subscribe_failures / _circuit_breaker_opened, carrying BOTH CCUs' traffic; no mqtt_HouseB_* series is ever registered (Registry.upsert only creates names asked for, registry.go:86-94). confirmed.title: wsapi.json and the CommissioningWindow doc comment name a WS publisher that only the REST path has; a cluster-command open broadcasts nothing

confirmed.title: A failed classification-index rebuild is published as a coherent "all clear" security snapshot, with no degraded or unknown state on any surface
confirmed.claim: Service.RebuildIndex (internal/security/index.go:29-37) returns early with the SQLite error from loadOverrides (index.go:299-303, `s.stores.Sources.GetAll`) or loadEnrollment (index.go:315-322, `s.stores.Sensors.GetAll`) without touching `s.agg.sources`/`s.agg.active`. Every caller — Start() (service.go:161), AttachCentral (service.go:228), the debounced per-central rebuild in attachUnit (subscribe.go:69) — only logs the error (`s.log.Error(...)`) and continues; none retries, none marks the domain degraded, and the Service is never registered with the daemon-wide health.Tracker (no `Record("security", ...)` call anywhere under internal/security). aggregate.snapshot() (aggregate.go:209-218) then walks every hmenum.SecurityClass and OMITS any class with `Known == 0` "rather than published as permanently inactive" — by design, so an install genuinely without gas detectors doesn't fake a gas class. That design collapses onto a failed rebuild too: an index that has zero sources because RebuildIndex errored produces the exact same `Classes: {}` shape as an index that legitimately has zero sources. severity() (aggregate.go:169-197) folds an empty Classes map and an untouched `engineHealthy: true` (set once in newAggregate(), aggregate.go:87, never flipped by an index-build failure) into hmenum.SecuritySeverityOK. Start() then calls `s.publishState(s.Snapshot())` (service.go:180) which fires SecurityStateChangedEvent{To: SecuritySeverityOK, ActiveClasses: nil, OpenFaults: 0} onto the domain bus that MQTT/REST/WS read from.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SQLite briefly errors on the security_sources or alarm_sensors table read (lock contention from a concurrent migration/backup, a disk-full write that also blocks reads, or a WAL checkpoint stall) at the moment RebuildIndex runs — either at Start() or from the debounced per-central rebuild once a CCU with enrolled smoke/water/door sensors reports southbound-ready. RebuildIndex returns the SQLite error, the service logs one Error line among the boot log volume and moves on. `s.agg.sources` stays empty (or stale from before the failure). The REST security snapshot, the MQTT `security/state` retained payload and the SPA security dashboard all show Severity=ok, no active classes, no open faults, EngineHealthy=true — indistinguishable from "no security-relevant devices configured" — while the physical smoke/door/water sensors are in fact unmonitored because the index that turns their events into a class was never built. Nothing on /health, in the REST payload, or in MQTT tells the operator the classification failed; only a single log line does, transient and easy to miss, and if the underlying condition persists (e.g. disk full) the domain stays silently blind indefinitely since only a model change or operator override edit triggers the next rebuild attempt.

(1) The reads are real and failable: SecuritySourceStore.GetAll runs db.QueryContext (SQLITE_BUSY past busy_timeout(5000), IO/disk-full, corruption) and RebuildIndex returns before any s.agg mutation, so a first-rebuild failure leaves sources empty. (3) The empty index really collapses to OK: classSeverity returns SecuritySeverityOK for any !st.Active class, severity() folds only those plus faults plus engineHealthy, and engineHealthy is the ALARM engine's verdict (set true in newAggregate, only ever written by onAlarmHealthChanged) - no index-health input exists, and hmenum has no 'unknown' severity at all. snapshot() then omits every Known==0 class, so the payload is byte-identical to 'this house has no detectors'. confirmed.claim: Logs.svelte dedupes incoming SSE records with `r.seq > lastSeq` and only ever raises lastSeq. The daemon's sequence counter is per-process in-memory state (pkg/hmlog/livelog.go:58 `seq uint64`, :90-91 `l.seq++; rec.Seq = l.seq`, allocated fresh in NewLiveLog), so it restarts at 1 on every daemon restart. Every post-restart record has seq <= the client's lastSeq and is dropped, while the reconnect fires the `open` handler which sets sseLive = true (Logs.svelte:193-196).

confirmed.claim: The per-row override draft is never seeded from server state: draftFor() returns `drafts[ref] ?? freshDraft()` and freshDraft() is hard-coded to `{ class: "", included: true, note: "" }` (SecuritySources.svelte:106-107, 110-112). The Switch renders `checked={d.included}` (:369-372), so a source the operator previously excluded still renders with the toggle ON. saveOverride() then always sends `included: d.included` (:127) instead of omitting the field, and the daemon maps a present `included:true` straight onto the stored override (internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:329-333), which sets `src.relevant = false` -> true again (internal/security/index.go:215, :268-269). Days later they reload the page: the row's include toggle is rendered ON, contradicting the stored state. They pick a different class for the same row (or just add a note) and press Save. The PUT carries included:true, the exclusion is dropped without any warning, the source re-enters the aggregates and starts raising security faults again. confirmed.title: needsCentralPrefix omits CUxD addresses, so two CCUs publish identical unique_ids for their CUxD data points
confirmed.claim: routingkey.GenerateUniqueID only prepends the central discriminator for the four hub pseudo-addresses, the INT000* prefix, and the three virtual-remote roots (BidCoS-RF, BidCoS-Wir, HmIP-RCV-1). CUxD device addresses are not in that set, yet they are allocated locally by the CUxD add-on on each CCU (shape `CUX<device-type><sequence>`, e.g. CUX2800001) and carry no CCU-specific component, so they repeat verbatim across CCUs. The resulting unique_id therefore has no central dimension at all. NeedsCentralScope() — the guard discovery.go consults before publishing without a serial — returns false for these addresses, so the publish is not even suppressed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two CCUs, `haus` and `garage`, are both configured with the CUxD interface (a first-class MVP interface per CLAUDE.md). Both have a CUxD switch at CUX2800001:1 with parameter STATE. MQTT discovery publishes two distinct retained config topics (`homeassistant/switch/haus_cux2800001/1_state/config` and `.../garage_cux2800001/1_state/config`) whose payloads both contain `"unique_id":"cux2800001_1_state"`. Home Assistant registers the first and rejects the second with 'Platform mqtt does not generate unique IDs', so one CCU's CUxD entities never appear. Because the discovery config is retained at QoS1, the loss survives daemon and HA restarts. REST reports the same duplicated id, so a client keying its registry on unique_id (the documented contract) also collapses the two devices into one.
confirmed.evidence: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:31-34 `var virtualRemoteRoots = map[string]struct{}{"BidCoS-RF": {}, "BidCoS-Wir": {}, "HmIP-RCV-1": {}}`; :101-110 needsCentralPrefix checks only centralPrefixAddresses / internalAddressPrefix / virtualRemoteRoots; :132-134 `if needsCentralPrefix(address) { uid = centralID + "_" + uid }`. The doc-comment at :86-95 names exactly this failure ('two CCUs would otherwise declare the identical id, and the consumer keeps whichever arrived first. Home Assistant does exactly that, and the payload is retained, so the loss outlives the daemon that caused it') — CUxD is simply missing from the set. Consumers: internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:503 `uniqueID, scoped := d.scopedUniqueID(ev.Central, chAddr, keyParameter, "")` → :528 `"unique_id": uniqueID`, and internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:1446-1452 scopedUniqueID, which only refuses to publish when NeedsCentralScope(address) is true; internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:943 `s.UniqueID = routingkey.CanonicalUniqueID(serialSuffix, k.ChannelAddress, string(dp.Parameter()), "")`. Address shape corroborated by the reference stack: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/central/events/integration.py:119 `device_addresses=("CUX2800001", "CUX2800002")` and ../aiohomematic/tests/test_central_device_coordinator.py:1281 `"ADDRESS": "CUX0000001:1"` — no serial component. Contrast pkg/hmtypes/wire_interface_id.go:34-37, which lists the repeating-address families as 'BidCoS-RF:1, INT000*, VCU virtual remotes' and likewise leaves CUxD out. The MQTT state/command topics DO carry the central (internal/north/mqtt/topics.go:86-118), so only the unique_id collides — which is precisely the field HA de-duplicates on.

NeedsCentralScope is the same predicate, so discovery.go:1446-1452 does not suppress the publish either. Address shape corroborated independently in godevccu (binrpc_test.go:40 `CUX2801001:1`) and aiohomematic (`CUX2800001`, `CUX0000001:1`): CUX + 4-digit device type + a per-CCU 3-digit counter, no CCU component — two CCUs each running CUxD with the same device type collide. confirmed.title: The audit trail persists no central_name; the CCU is reconstructed at read time from the live device model and is lost once the device or CCU is gone
confirmed.claim: audit_log has no central_name column and audit.Entry has no central field, so every write-side producer (paramset write, link add/remove/update, link-paramset write, link activate) records only a device address. GET /api/v1/audit reconstructs the CCU by looking the address up in the *current* device model. That reconstruction is not persisted, so it is only correct while the device is still present on exactly one central: a device unpaired, replaced or belonging to a CCU that has since been removed yields central="" forever after, and the `?central=<name>` filter then silently drops the row rather than reporting it as unattributable. ADR 0002 lists central_name as a first-class dimension 'for debugging, filtering, and diagnostics'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a two-CCU daemon an operator writes a MASTER paramset on device MEQ0123456:1 of central `garage`; one row is appended with device_address=MEQ0123456 and no central. Weeks later the device is replaced via the guided device-replace flow (or the `garage` CCU is deleted through DELETE /api/v1/centrals/garage). Opening the change history with ?central=garage now returns nothing for that write — applyAuditFilter derives centralName="" because CentralOf finds no device with that address, and the `f.centralName != "" && centralName != f.centralName` test drops the entry. The unfiltered view shows the row with an empty `central` field, so a fleet operator cannot tell which CCU was reconfigured. The information was available at write time and was simply never stored.

The schema has no central column (002_audit.sql:4-16, and it is the ONLY migration that touches audit_log — no later ALTER), audit.Entry has no central field (audit.go:268-292), and the INSERT column list matches (sqlite/audit.go:81-96). confirmed.title: Removing or disabling a CCU retracts its device entities but never its hub-plane MQTT discovery configs, and no later sweep can reach them
confirmed.claim: removeCentral evicts the device model (which the event bridge turns into MQTT retractions — the code comments say so explicitly and order detachBridge after the eviction for exactly that reason) but nothing evicts the removed central's hub entities. Hub.RemoveProgram / Hub.RemoveSysvar are the only callers of the Program/Sysvar NotifyRemoved hooks the hub publisher subscribes to for retraction, and removeCentral calls neither; HubMQTTPublisher.Stop only drops subscriptions. The automatic discovery-orphan sweep cannot clean up afterwards either: it is invoked once per *registered* central and scopes its filter to that central's node-id prefixes, so a name that is no longer in the registry is never passed in.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A fleet operator deletes CCU `garage` in the SPA (DELETE /api/v1/centrals/garage) or flips it to enabled=false. HA re-creates all of them on the next integration reload and they stay permanently unavailable. On the next daemon boot the orphan sweep runs for the remaining centrals only, so `garage_*` is classified 'not our namespace — skip' and survives; the only remedy is a manual broker purge.

confirmed.title: MQTT select/enum writes send the option token verbatim; every ENUM parameter in the fleet is index-based, so the whole MQTT select write surface is mis-encoded
confirmed.claim: The per-parameter command handler coerces the payload with parseCommandPayload, which is descriptor-blind (command_subscriber.go:874 and :913 -> :1314). For an ENUM parameter the payload is neither a bool token nor numeric, so it falls through to the final `return s` and reaches the sink as a Go string. MQTTCommandSink.SetValue hands it to ch.Writer().SetValue unchanged (internal/central/adapter/mqtt_sink.go:120-128) and MQTTCommandSink.SetMasterValue wraps it with hmtypes.NewParamValue, which maps string -> StringValue with no enum lookup (mqtt_sink.go:198-206; pkg/hmtypes/value.go:119-120). device.Channel.Set is called with SetOptions{Optimistic:true} i.e. Validate=false, so validateForSet is skipped and `wireVal := v.Unwrap()` (internal/model/device/channel_set.go:333-358) forwards the string into dispatchSet -> PutParamset/SetValue (channel_set.go:583-586). ValueWriter.SetValue leaves CheckAgainstPD false (internal/client/value_writer.go:157-167), and setValueViaCaller marshals `value any` by its Go type onto XML-RPC (internal/client/backends/wire_shared.go:169-182). No layer converts the token to its index. Every other write surface does: REST PUT /value calls parameter.Coerce (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:806) whose coerceEnum returns IntValue(indexOf(ValueList,s)) (internal/parameter/coerce.go:92-105); the REST paramset path does the same (internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:283,583); the typed DP converts via Select.SetLabel -> SetIndex (internal/model/generic/select.go:62-73). The daemon's own MQTT read path proves the wire form is an index: ResolveEnumLabel turns the int index into the label before publishing (internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1998-2007). The flag that exists precisely to decide index-vs-string, DataPoint.EnumValueIsIndex (internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1952, mirroring aiohomematic's _enum_value_is_index), has no production caller at all.

Discovery declares component=select, options=[analog_output,digital_output], command_topic=<base>/<central>/HmIP-RF/VCU0000002/10/master/BEHAVIOUR/set, command_template={{ value | upper }} (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:858-866; verified verbatim in the fleet discovery snapshot). The operator picks 'digital_output' in Home Assistant; HA publishes the string DIGITAL_OUTPUT. The daemon issues putParamset(MASTER, {"BEHAVIOUR": <string>DIGITAL_OUTPUT</string>}) instead of the integer 1 the descriptor's integer MIN marks as index-based. The CCU rejects it (or stores garbage); the only trace is a Warn 'mqtt.command.setmasterparam'. The identical edit made through the SPA/REST sends index 1 and succeeds. The fleet snapshot carries 1489 select entities across 20 distinct ENUM parameters (MSG_FOR_POS_A/B, REPEATED_LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT_UNIT, EVENT_DELAY_UNIT, POWERUP_ACTION, BEHAVIOUR, INPUT_TYPE, ...), so the whole select surface of the MQTT plane is affected, not one device.

confirmed.claim: physicalDeviceIdentifier builds the HA `device.identifiers` value as "openccu-loom_" + lower(deviceAddress) with no central segment, and deviceDescriptor stamps it on every per-DP, press-button and device-linked hub payload. The daemon already knows this address class is not unique across CCUs and handles it everywhere else: routingkey.NeedsCentralScope lists exactly HubAddress/InstallMode/Program/Sysvar, INT000* and the virtual-remote roots BidCoS-RF / BidCoS-Wir / HmIP-RCV-1 (internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:26-110); scopedUniqueID refuses to publish those without the CCU serial and its doc comment reasons about precisely this collision; DiscoveryNodeID prefixes the central slug; centralDeviceIdentifier is central-scoped. confirmed.failure_scenario: Two CCUs are adopted. Both expose heating groups at INT0000001 (every CCU numbers them from INT0000001; the fleet snapshot contains such devices) and both expose the virtual remote HmIP-RCV-1. The merged card takes the name, model, sw_version, configuration_url and via_device of whichever CCU published last, so it nests under the wrong CCU and its 'Visit device' button opens the wrong CCU's WebUI; every republish can flip it.

confirmed.title: Brute-force protection covers only POST /auth/login — the same passwords can be guessed at unlimited rate via HTTP Basic on any route
confirmed.claim: The per-IP login speed-bump is attached to exactly one route (`r.With(d.LoginRateLimit.Middleware()).Post("/auth/login", login)`, router.go:706, plus `/auth/oidc/start` at :724). HTTP Basic is a fully equivalent credential surface: `auth.Middleware.Resolve` is mounted globally on the root router (router.go:606-608) and `resolve()` runs `m.Users.AuthenticateBasic` for ANY request that carries an `Authorization: Basic` header (internal/auth/middleware.go:89-99), on every path, with no limiter. Basic is on by default — `BasicAuthEnabled()` returns `orDefault(a.BasicEnabled, true)` (internal/config/config.go:1515-1517) — and the store it hits is the full login chain incl. the SQLite users and (in the add-on build, CCU-delegated login first) the CCU user database: `gatedAuthMiddleware(cfg, loginChainWithCCU(d.sqUsers, d.users, ccuStore, ccuPrimary), ...)` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest.go:217-221). The only other throttle, `middleware.RateLimit`, is (a) keyed on the resolved identity so every failed attempt shares one "anonymous" bucket rather than a per-source one (internal/north/rest/middleware/ratelimit.go:104-112) and (b) OFF BY DEFAULT: `buildRateLimitConfig` returns nil unless `rl.Enabled` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:741-745) and `NorthRESTRateLimit.Enabled` defaults to false (internal/config/config.go:1216-1219). There is no per-account lockout, no failed-attempt counter, and no audit record for a failed Basic attempt. The router comment at :701-703 asserts the opposite of the code: "the SPA is the sole login surface, so this is the one place a sweep can guess credentials".
confirmed.failure_scenario: Attacker on the LAN runs `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -u admin:<guess> http://<daemon>:8119/api/v1/auth/me` in a loop. 200 means the password is correct (the body additionally returns subject + role, handlers.Me(), internal/north/rest/handlers/auth.go:310-323); 401 means wrong. No rate limit, no lockout, no log of the attempt above debug. The `/auth/login` limiter (1 req/s per IP, burst 5) is never consulted because a different route is used. Same guessing works against the CCU's own user database when CCU-delegated auth is on (default in the add-on, `ccuAuthEnabled` -> `build.IsAddon()`, cmd/openccu-loom/ccu_auth_wiring.go:25-30). Secondary effect: because the unknown-user path deliberately runs a dummy bcrypt at cost 12 (internal/auth/auth.go:340-344, bcryptCost=12 at :293), each such request costs a full bcrypt on the daemon — an unauthenticated caller can pin every core with a few hundred concurrent Basic requests, including against rate-limit-exempt paths like `/api/v1/health` (SkipPaths, ratelimit.go:49-53).

Defaults to false`); internal/north/rest/middleware/ratelimit.go:104-112 (`identityKey` -> "anonymous"); internal/auth/auth.go:293,340-344 (bcryptCost 12 + dummy compare on unknown user).
confirmed.verifier_reason: Reproduced end to end. Exact attacker request: `GET /api/v1/auth/me` with `Authorization: Basic base64(user:guess)` (any route works; /auth/me is the cleanest oracle because it sits outside the AuthRequire group, router.go:711). I built the real router with a memory user store, the auth middleware as AuthResolve and a live LoginRateLimiter, then fired 500 wrong-password Basic probes from one IP: result `map[401:500]` — not a single 429. The same 30 probes against POST /api/v1/auth/login gave `map[429:25 503:5]`. A correct password returned `200 {"subject":"admin","role":"admin","scheme":"basic"}` — a perfect success oracle. Temp test deleted. Every middleware in the chain checked (router.go:592-621): decodedPathRouting, RequestID, SecurityHeaders, ReqContextWithCentral, Logger, Recover, timeout, StatusCounter, CORS, AuthResolve, Idempotency, CSRF, RateLimit — none throttles by source. auth/middleware.go:89-99 runs Users.AuthenticateBasic on every request carrying a Basic header; Basic defaults ON (config.go:1515-1517 `orDefault(a.BasicEnabled, true)`); the only other limiter is off by default (daemon_north.go:741-745 `if !rl.Enabled { return nil }`, config.go:1216-1219) and is keyed on the resolved identity, so failures all share the single "anonymous" bucket (ratelimit.go:104-112). No lockout and no failed-attempt counter exists anywhere in internal/auth (the only lockout ledgers in the tree are the alarm code plane and Matter PASE). The store behind it is the full login chain incl. confirmed.title: Logout revokes the session record but leaves the user's already-open WebSocket fully privileged
confirmed.claim: A WebSocket connection captures its identity once at upgrade and gates every later command on that snapshot; the code states the only way a revocation reaches an open socket is from the other side (internal/north/rest/ws/handler.go:143-151, `// A revocation reaches the socket from the other side instead — see [Hub.CloseBySubject]`). The daemon therefore wraps its session revoker in `ws.RevokeWithSockets(d.sessions, d.wsHub)` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:627-631), and admin user-update, user-delete and self-service password change all go through it (router.go:1317-1318, :789), as does bearer-token delete via `tokenSocketRevoker()` (:641-646, router.go:1323-1324). `Logout` does not: it calls the raw `*auth.SessionStore` directly — `d.Sessions.Revoke(c.Value)` — so `Hub.CloseBySubject` never runs and the socket keeps dispatching operator/admin commands.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An attacker who obtained an operator's session cookie (shared machine, proxy log, XSS on a co-hosted origin) opens `GET /api/v1/events` with it; the upgrade succeeds and the socket snapshots the operator identity. The victim notices and does the one remediation the SPA offers — Log out. `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` deletes the session id, so the attacker's REST calls now 401, but the attacker's WebSocket is untouched and keeps accepting `{"command":"alarm_panel.disarm"}`, `{"command":"paramset.put"}`, `{"command":"sysvars.set"}` for as long as the connection is held open. Only an admin editing/deleting the account (or a password change) actually closes it.
confirmed.evidence: internal/north/rest/handlers/auth.go:297-304 (`func Logout(d *AuthDeps) ... d.Sessions.Revoke(c.Value)` — no socket hook); internal/north/rest/ws/handler.go:143-151 (identity captured once at upgrade; comment names Hub.CloseBySubject as the only teardown); internal/north/rest/ws/credential_revocation.go:36-74 (`RevokeWithSockets` -> `r.sockets.CloseBySubject(subject)`); cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:621-646 (both socket-aware revokers, and the comment stating why: "a socket captures its identity at the upgrade ... leaves the old role live on the command plane"); router.go:710 (`r.Post("/auth/logout", handlers.Logout(d.Auth))` — passed `d.Auth`, not the composed revoker).
confirmed.verifier_reason: Exact request: POST /api/v1/auth/logout with the session cookie. Handler calls the concrete store directly — `d.Sessions.Revoke(c.Value)` (auth.go:297-304), and AuthDeps.Sessions is the concrete *auth.SessionStore (auth.go:25), so no socket-aware wrapper can be injected there; router.go:710 passes d.Auth, not d.SessionRevoker. What the caller gets afterwards: REST 401s, but the already-open socket keeps its upgrade-time identity snapshot (handler.go:142-151) and every command is gated on that snapshot alone — client.go:709-715 injects c.Identity() into the dispatch context and the session store is never re-consulted, so operator/admin verbs keep working for the life of the connection. The socket-teardown composition exists and is used by every sibling revocation (daemon_rest_mount.go:621-646; router.go:1317-1318 user update/delete, :789 self-service password change, :1323-1324 token delete). No ADR, doc or comment records the omission as deliberate (docs/admin/auth.md:102 simply says logout 'revokes the session'). One genuine nuance the claim omits: sockets carry no session id, so the only available teardown is CloseBySubject, which would also drop that user's other tabs/devices (they reconnect with their still-valid cookie). Medium: exploitation presupposes a stolen cookie / attacker-held socket, but logout is the remediation the SPA offers and it does not terminate the privileged channel.

confirmed.title: WS recording.start/stop are operator-gated while the identical REST route is admin-gated, and the WS path writes no audit row and arms no auto-stop
confirmed.claim: `writeCommandRoles` maps `recording.start` / `recording.stop` to `auth.RoleOperator` (internal/north/rest/ws/commands.go:107-108) while the REST twin `POST /diagnostics/rpc-recording` (+ `/stop`) is mounted `.With(admin)` (internal/north/rest/router.go:1161-1162). Both drive the same object: the WS handler calls `u.Recorder.StartSession()` on every registered central (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:1272-1281, `wsSessionRecorder.Start`), which is exactly what `RPCRecorderAdapter.Start` does (internal/central/adapter/rpc_recorder.go:113-126). The table's own doc-comment states the policy this violates — the admin tier exists because those commands "mirror the REST ... routes" (commands.go:36-38), and `ccu.get_rssi_info` is pinned to admin explicitly because "GET /diagnostics/rssi refuses to anyone below admin" (commands.go:127-131). The WS path also skips both safeguards the REST handler applies: no `auditRecord(rec, r, actionRPCRecordingStart, ...)` (handlers/diagnostics_rpc_recorder.go:63) and no `armLocked` auto-stop timer bounded by `rpcRecordingMaxDuration` (rpc_recorder.go:129-140), so the capture stays armed until someone stops it.

confirmed.title: HA master-panel DISARM burns the shared MQTT code rate-limit budget and then locks out correct per-zone PINs
confirmed.claim: MasterDisarm/MasterArm are documented as code-free, but they do not skip the code check — they call the code-free verb wrapper for every zone, so each armed zone with an effective code requirement produces one ErrInvalidCode inside the codes facade and one recordFailure against the *source string* "mqtt". The rate limiter is keyed by source only, not by zone, and Facade.Validate consults it before it ever compares a supplied code. Five accumulated failures lock the whole `mqtt` source out for 60 s, doubling per lockout up to 15 min; while locked, a per-zone disarm carrying the CORRECT PIN is refused with ErrInvalidCode before any candidate is verified. Failures only decay on a successful validate, which is unreachable while locked.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An installation with 5 armed zones and one enabled PIN code (zones: [] = all zones, RequireDisarm at its nil default = required). The operator presses DISARM on the HA aggregate `master` alarm_control_panel — HA sends one DISARM to <base>/alarm/master/set, with no code, because the master discovery config is built with code_disarm_required=false (alarm_publisher.go:482). MasterDisarm loops all 5 zones -> 5x recordFailure("mqtt") -> lockout. The operator now presses DISARM on an individual zone panel and types the correct PIN: Validate returns ErrInvalidCode from the lockout branch, the siren keeps sounding, and the journal records `code_locked_out` instead of a disarm. confirmed.title: Any verified output stop reports the whole alarm domain healthy again, erasing a failed-fire degradation (S7)
confirmed.claim: The only healthy-recovery signal in the alarm domain is unconditional and un-scoped: verifyStop reports health(true) for the manager as a whole whenever ANY single output's stop read-back succeeds. The health tracker is last-sample-wins per component name ("alarm"), so that one success overwrites the degradation an unrelated — or even the same — output raised when its fire command failed. Nothing aggregates the outstanding failures, and there is no per-output health scope.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A zone triggers. The acoustic siren's write fails (device unreachable): Manager.outputFailed journals `output_fire_failed` and records health{Healthy:false} -> /api/v1/health shows alarm degraded and AlarmHealthChangedEvent{false} marks every panel unavailable. Nothing else changes. Anyone then presses SILENCE (or the trigger window elapses -> finishTriggered -> StopAll), which runs stopAndVerify over every stoppable output of the zone. Ten seconds later verifyStop reads the plug back as off — it never turned on — returns stopped=true and records health{Healthy:true, Note:"alarm output stop verified"}. /api/v1/health reports the alarm domain healthy while the siren that did not sound is still unreachable; the security domain adopts engineHealthy=true too (internal/security/subscribe.go:554-560). The only surface that told the operator to look at all is cleared within one incident, which is the exact silent-failure mode S7 exists to prevent.

The degradation side: internal/alarm/outputs/manager.go:612-632 outputFailed -> `m.health(false, note)` with the doc "A command that only journals leaves /api/v1/health reporting the alarm domain healthy while a siren did not go off". `grep -n "m.health(" internal/alarm/outputs/*.go` returns exactly manager.go:631 (false), watchdog.go:121 (true), watchdog.go:129 (false) — watchdog.go:121 is the only recovery path and it is per-stop, not per-domain. Last-sample-wins: internal/health/tracker.go:206-214 `t.components[name] = Component{Name: name, Status: status, LastSample: sample}` and cmd/openccu-loom/alarm_wiring.go:32-34 `tracker.Record("alarm", health.Sample{Healthy: healthy, Note: note})` — one component for the whole domain. The alarm service fans the same call onto the bus without aggregation: internal/alarm/service.go:135-143. The stop verify runs 10 s after the stop write (internal/alarm/outputs/config.go:26-28 stopVerifyInterval = 10*time.Second). No test covers the erasure: internal/alarm/outputs/failure_visibility_test.go asserts only that the *last* sample is unhealthy immediately after the failed fire (assertUnhealthy, :108-123).
confirmed.verifier_reason: Whole chain verified. watchdog.go:116-123 is the sole recovery signal and it is unconditional and un-scoped; grep confirms exactly three health calls in the package (manager.go:631 false, watchdog.go:121 true, watchdog.go:129 false). confirmed.title: The duress journal row can never be read back: AlarmJournalFilter.IncludeHidden has no production caller
confirmed.claim: fireDuress persists the covert-trigger record as a Hidden journal row, and AlarmJournalStore.Query filters `hidden = 0` unless the caller opts in via IncludeHidden. No production code ever sets IncludeHidden — the only writers of that field in the whole tree are tests. The duress record is therefore write-only: it is retained in SQLite, purged by retention, and unreachable from REST, WS, MCP, the SPA journal and the CSV export. The struct doc promises the opposite ("stay out of user-visible surfaces until resolved but are fully retained") and names a resolution/opt-in path that does not exist.
confirmed.failure_scenario: alarm.duress_visibility = hidden (a documented, validated level) on an installation with no webhook configured — the setup the config help text itself describes as "nobody is told at all". Someone disarms under coercion with the duress code. The engine writes the Hidden journal row (actor, source, verb, incident id) and publishes AlarmDuressEvent; the security domain drops it at the visibility gate, MQTT never subscribed, the WS never subscribed. Afterwards the operator or the police want the record: GET /api/v1/alarm/journal (and the WS alarm_panel.journal command, and the SPA journal view) all go through Query with IncludeHidden unset, so the row is filtered out on every surface. The audit.Recorder row for the same action says only "alarm.disarm". The event leaves no readable trace anywhere.
confirmed.evidence: internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:645-659 fireDuress -> `e.journalEntry(ctx, a, JournalEntry{..., Hidden: true})`. internal/alarm/journal/journal.go:52-78 persists Hidden and suppresses the append event. internal/store/sqlite/alarm_journal.go:44-52 `IncludeHidden bool` and :102-105 `if !f.IncludeHidden { where = append(where, "hidden = 0") }`, with the type doc at :17-20 "they stay out of user-visible surfaces until resolved but are fully retained, so Query excludes them unless the caller explicitly opts in". `grep -rn "IncludeHidden" --include=*.go .` outside the store file returns only test files: internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm_verb_code_test.go:188, internal/alarm/intents_test.go:125, internal/alarm/inputs_connectivity_test.go:277, internal/alarm/sysvar_test.go:468, internal/store/sqlite/alarm_journal_test.go:246. confirmed.verifier_reason: fireDuress writes the row with Hidden: true unconditionally (engine.go:645-652) and Query appends `hidden = 0` unless IncludeHidden is set (alarm_journal.go:102-105). Checked every reader myself: the REST filter builder (alarm.go:558-599 — zone/class/from/to/limit only, no include_hidden query parameter in openapi.yaml) and the WS alarm_panel.journal filter (alarm_panel.go:293-312) both leave it false; there is no MCP journal tool, and the SPA's CSV export is built client-side from the fetched rows (AlarmJournal.svelte:178-204), so it inherits the exclusion. confirmed.title: Every structured attribute write except AccessControl.ACL decodes to a nil value, so GroupKeyMap and AccessControl.Extension writes always fail
confirmed.claim: attributeValueReader is a hand-maintained switch with exactly one structured case: `if path.Cluster == 0x001F && path.Attribute == 0x0000 { return decodeACLList(el, dec) }` (attribute_value_reader.go:31-33). Everything else falls through to primitiveAttributeValue, which for a container does `skipContainerTLV(dec); return im.AttributeValue{}, nil` (attribute_value_reader.go:212-216) — the array is drained and a nil Value is handed on. Three mounted, writable, list-typed attributes have no case: GroupKeyManagement.GroupKeyMap (0x003F/0x0000) whose handler asserts `value.([]GroupKeyMapStruct)` (group_key_management.go:327-330), AccessControl.Extension (0x001F/0x0001) whose handler asserts `value.([]AccessControlExtensionEntry)` (access_control.go:598-601), and Binding (dead, see C7-matter-parity-5). endpoint/dispatcher.go:565-573 passes value.Value straight into MatterWrite, so the assertion fails on nil; the resulting message matches no branch of writeErrorStatus (dispatcher.go:606-620) and the controller gets StatusFailure (0x01). matter.js does not maintain a switch: AttributeWriteResponse.ts:421-423 decodes with the attribute's own TlvSchema (`this.#decodeWithSchema(tlv, value)`), so every list/struct attribute is decodable by construction.
confirmed.failure_scenario: GroupKeyManagement is mounted on the root endpoint (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:2277-2282 appends `gkm` to the root cluster set) and GroupKeyMap is writable (group_key_management.go:323-326 rejects only *other* attribute ids as read-only). A controller configuring Matter multicast groups — chip-tool `groupkeymanagement write group-key-map`, python-matter-server / Home Assistant Matter, any group-cast setup — writes the list; the bridge answers FAILURE for every write, so no group key binding is ever established and group-cast commands never reach the bridge. AccessControl.Extension is advertised in AttributeList (access_control.go:656) with the same outcome. The full replace-semantics implementation behind both (store writes, dropped-binding removal, DataVersion bump, 128-byte constraint checks) is unreachable from the wire.
confirmed.evidence: internal/north/matter/bridge/attribute_value_reader.go:30-35 `func attributeValueReader(...) { if path.Cluster == 0x001F && path.Attribute == 0x0000 { return decodeACLList(el, dec) }; return primitiveAttributeValue(el, dec) }`; :212-216 `if el.IsContainer { if err := skipContainerTLV(dec); ...; return im.AttributeValue{}, nil }`. internal/north/matter/cluster/core/group_key_management.go:327 `list, ok := value.([]GroupKeyMapStruct); if !ok { return fmt.Errorf("%w: GroupKeyMap write expected []GroupKeyMapStruct, got %T", ...) }`. internal/north/matter/cluster/core/access_control.go:598. Mount point: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:2277-2282. Status mapping: internal/north/matter/endpoint/dispatcher.go:569-573 + 597-622 (no heuristic matches -> im.StatusFailure). Gold standard: ../matter.js/packages/protocol/src/action/server/AttributeWriteResponse.ts:421-427 (`const decoded = this.#decodeWithSchema(tlv, value); writeState[attributeId] = decoded`). The read direction works and hides the asymmetry: internal/north/matter/bridge/reply_value_writer_test.go:262-267 encodes []GroupKeyMapStruct on the report path. Bracketing tests keep the gap green — internal/north/matter/cluster/core/group_key_management_test.go:316 calls `gkm.MatterWrite(ctx, 0x0000, mappings, ...)` with a Go []GroupKeyMapStruct the wire path can never produce; no bridge-level test drives a 0x003F write through UnmarshalWriteRequestTLV.
confirmed.verifier_reason: Proven with a scratch test in package bridge: a well-formed GroupKeyMap array (0x003F/0x0000) and a well-formed AccessControl.Extension array (0x001F/0x0001) both come back from attributeValueReader as `value=<nil> isNull=false err=<nil>` - the container is drained by primitiveAttributeValue (attribute_value_reader.go:205-216) because the switch has exactly one structured case (:31-33). The consumers assert concrete list types (group_key_management.go:327-330, access_control.go:598-601), so the write returns a plain error whose text matches no branch of writeErrorStatus (dispatcher.go:597-620) and the controller sees StatusFailure. The wire path is the production one (bridge/receive.go:406 `im.UnmarshalWriteRequestTLV(dec, attributeValueReader)`), GroupKeyManagement is mounted on the root endpoint by buildRootClusters (daemon_matter.go:2277-2282), and dispatcher.go:564-570 hands value.Value straight through. The matter.js citation holds: packages/protocol/src/action/server/AttributeWriteResponse.ts:421-427 decodes with the attribute's own TlvSchema, so no per-attribute switch can drift. Rated medium rather than high: the mechanism is certain, but no mainstream controller flow was shown to write these attributes (Apple's post-commissioning ACL write, the one that does matter, is the single handled case), so the observable loss is that Matter group-cast configuration and AC extensions are unusable, not a pairing abort.

confirmed.title: The discovery-orphan sweep matches node-id prefixes without an underscore boundary, so a central whose slug prefixes another's evicts that other CCU's retained discovery configs
confirmed.claim: RunDiscoveryOrphanCleanupOnce classifies a retained config as 'ours' with hasAnyPrefix(nodeID, discoveryNodePrefixes(rawCentral)), i.e. strings.HasPrefix(nodeID, "<slug>_"). Node ids are "<central-slug>_<address-lower>", so for central 'CCU' the prefix is "ccu_" and central 'CCU Wohnung' produces node ids "ccu_wohnung_<addr>" - which start with "ccu_". The per-central sweep is documented to run right after that central's own snapshot ('the other centrals' entities are not in `declared` yet and must not be judged'), so the second CCU's retained configs are matched, found absent from `declared`, and cleared. The raw-plane twin does not have this hole because rawCentralPrefix ends the segment with '/': "loom/ccu_wohnung/..." does not start with "loom/ccu/". The fix is an underscore-boundary check on the remainder (the address is hex, so requiring the rest to contain no further '_' or matching "<slug>_<hex>$" both work). Note: this predates commit c706d9d7; the wave hardened the neighbouring retraction path (RetractDiscoveryForCentralDevice, which anchors on "/"+prefix+addr+"/" and is therefore safe) but left the sweep's prefix test unchanged.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two CCUs named 'CCU' and 'CCU Wohnung'. On boot 'CCU' passes its readiness gate first, publishes its snapshot, and its post-snapshot hook runs RunDiscoveryOrphanCleanupOnce("CCU"). 'CCU Wohnung' is still waiting for its CCU, so none of its entities are in `declared`. Every retained homeassistant/<component>/ccu_wohnung_<addr>/<obj>/config left by the previous boot matches prefix "ccu_", is judged an orphan, and gets an empty retained payload - Home Assistant removes every entity of the second CCU. They only come back if and when that CCU finishes its own snapshot; if it stays offline they are gone until a later boot with both CCUs up.

confirmed.title: A recovered boot-time MQTT connect gets no reconnect loop: the retry goroutine cancels the context the new lifecycle (and the hub fan-out and the health probe) runs on
confirmed.claim: retryInitialConnect derives retryCtx from the daemon ctx and hands it to Swap (line 415). Swap -> buildSwap(ctx,newCfg) (line 469) -> sw.lifecycle.Start(ctx) (line 578). go-mqtt's Lifecycle.Start does `runCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)` and then runs the whole reconnect loop on runCtx (`go func(){ l.loop(runCtx) }()`), and loop's first select is `case <-ctx.Done(): return`. The retry goroutine's deferred `cancel()` (mqtt_supervisor.go:397-402) fires the instant Swap returns nil, so runCtx is cancelled milliseconds after the recovered stack is committed and the reconnect loop exits before it ever runs. Nothing re-arms it: Start is never called again on that lifecycle, and s.current is non-nil so the retry loop will not re-enter either. The same cancelled ctx is also what announceConnected (line 484) hands to the OnConnect hooks, and adapter.HubMQTTPublisher.Start captures it inside its long-lived Metrics.OnUpdate closures (internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:343-400), so every later hub publish carries a dead context. NOTE: this shape is byte-identical at 89d513f1, i.e. it is not introduced by c706d9d7 — but it is not in known_findings_index.txt, it sits in the file this wave reworked most, and the wave's surrounding work (ensureWiring/announceConnected) is precisely what makes the deferred-connect path reachable and load-bearing.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Daemon and a co-located Mosquitto add-on start together; the broker is not accepting connections yet. mqttSup.Start fails, logs mqtt.supervisor.start, and arms retryInitialConnect. 5 s later the broker is up, Swap succeeds, `mqtt.supervisor.connect.recovered` is logged and MQTT publishes work — the operator sees a healthy plane. The retry goroutine then returns and cancels retryCtx, killing the lifecycle's reconnect loop. The next broker restart (add-on update, container restart, network blip) drops the session permanently: no reconnect attempt, no log line, MQTT/HA discovery dead until the daemon is restarted or an operator triggers POST /mqtt/reload.
