confirmed.title: The PASE brute-force lockout un-locks itself the first time it fires while a commissioning window is open (its own RevokeWindow runs the restore closure, which re-attaches a PASE acceptor and calls resetPaseFailures)
confirmed.claim: recordPaseFailure engages the lockout and then revokes the commissioning window in the same call. RevokeWindow runs the window's restore closure, every production restore closure re-attaches a PASE acceptor, and AttachPaseHandler/AttachPaseHandlerProvider unconditionally call resetPaseFailures(), which zeroes paseLockoutUntil AND paseLockoutStreak. The refusal added by this wave therefore lives for a few microseconds and the doubling backoff can never accumulate. This is known finding [CONFIRMED-medium] internal/north/matter/bridge/securechannel.go:488 ("PASE brute-force cap never stops PASE processing") only half fixed: it holds only when NO window is attached, which is exactly the case the new tests cover.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An Enhanced Commissioning Window is open (Apple/Google multi-admin OpenCommissioningWindow, or the REST 'open pairing window' ephemeral flow). A LAN host sends 20 malformed Pake1 datagrams. recordPaseFailure sets paseLockoutUntil = now+15m, then RevokeWindow -> restore() -> AttachPaseHandler(configured) -> resetPaseFailures() clears it. paseLockedOut() is false again before the next datagram arrives, the long-lived configured-passcode acceptor is back on the receive path, and guessing continues at full rate forever with streak stuck at 0 (no backoff). The operator-facing diagnostic event simultaneously claims 'Pairing was locked ... it unlocks again after the lockout period', which is false.

Proven with a throw-away test in package bridge that opens a window via openedWindow's OpenWindow and registers the production-shaped restore via w.setRestore(func(){ b.AttachPaseHandler(nil) }): after paseMaxErrors failures it logged `paseLockedOut = false`, `streak=0 failures=0` (the WARN matter.rx.sc.pase_bruteforce fired first, so the cap did trip). The three new guards never reach this path: securechannel_bruteforce_test.go:118 TestBridge_PaseLockedOutAtCap and :193 TestBridge_PaseLockoutExpiresOnItsOwn use newStartedBridge(t) with NO commissioning window (win==nil, so RevokeWindow is never called), and openedWindow (securechannel_bruteforce_test.go:26-38) never registers a restore closure.

confirmed.title: StartSession's new double-start guard has no honouring caller, so restarting an RPC recording keeps the previous trace and re-arms with the new options
confirmed.claim: internal/store/session/recorder.go now sets isRecording in StartSession (:142) and Resume (:153), so StartSession returns false and does NOT clear the store while a session is in progress. Both production callers discard the return value and continue as if a fresh session had begun: RPCRecorderAdapter.Start (rpc_recorder.go:120) then calls armLocked (:121) with the NEW duration/randomize and writeMarker (:124) with the new scope, and wsSessionRecorder.Start (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:1278) returns w.IsActive() (:1281) which is true because the OLD session is still active. Before this change StartSession always cleared, so the fix converted a working reset into a silent no-op on the operator's Start verb. Neither caller stops first, which is what the new doc comment tells callers to do.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Operator starts an RPC recording on ccu1 with randomize=true, then (without pressing Stop) presses Start again to capture a fresh trace with randomize=false — the SPA/REST offers exactly this. StartSession returns false, the store is not cleared, but armLocked installs the new auto-stop deadline and the new randomize flag and writeMarker persists the new marker. GET status reports a fresh recording. The subsequent export contains the earlier session's RPC traffic mixed with the new one, and is emitted un-anonymised because the current recState carries randomize=false. confirmed.title: MatchDuress charges a probe failure for the household's ordinary correct PIN, so repeated no-op MQTT disarms mute the covert duress channel
confirmed.claim: MatchDuress verifies ONLY duress rows (facade.go:233-238), so any code that is not the duress code — including a perfectly valid non-duress PIN — falls through the loop and reaches `f.probes.recordFailure(source, now)` (:260-262). The ledger is only ever cleared by `f.probes.recordSuccess(source)` on an actual duress match (:254-256). rateLimiter has no decay: fails is cumulative until it hits 5, then a lockout of 60s is engaged and `lockouts` is incremented, doubling the next lockout up to a 15 min cap (ratelimit.go:60-77, 89-98). So five ordinary code-carrying disarms of an already-disarmed zone from one non-operator source lock that source's probe budget, and each further five extend the lockout. During the lockout MatchDuress returns at :248-250 before verifying anything, i.e. a real duress code produces no journal row, no AlarmDuressEvent, no webhook — silently.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Installation with a duress code and a code-required disarm policy, driven from Home Assistant over MQTT (source "mqtt", which engine.IsOperatorSource does not cover, so limited=true). An HA automation or a re-delivered/duplicate MQTT command issues alarm_control_panel.alarm_disarm with the resident's correct PIN while the zone is already disarmed — a no-op by design. Each such call records a probe failure. After the fifth, the "mqtt" probe ledger is locked for 60s; after 40 lifetime occurrences it is locked for 15 minutes at a time. If the resident is then coerced and sends the duress PIN from HA while the zone is disarmed — precisely the scenario DisarmWithCode's new branch was added for — MatchDuress returns ('',false) and nothing is emitted anywhere.
confirmed.evidence: internal/alarm/codes/facade.go:233-238 only `c.duress` rows become candidates; :246-251 `limited := !engine.IsOperatorSource(source)` then `if allowed, _ := f.probes.allow(source, now); !allowed { return "", false }`; :252-262 `for _, c := range duressCandidates { if VerifyPIN(...) { f.probes.recordSuccess(source); ... } }` / `f.probes.recordFailure(source, now)`. internal/alarm/codes/ratelimit.go:19-22 `rateLimitMaxAttempts = 5`, base 60s, cap 15m; :68-76 fails is cumulative and lockouts grows. internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:703-709 the disarmed branch calls matchDuress with the supplied code; :76-83 IsOperatorSource covers only rest-operator/ws-operator/hmcli. cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:459 `alarmSourceMQTT = "mqtt"`; :499-501 `alarmMQTTSink.Disarm` -> `DisarmWithCode(ctx, zoneID, "", alarmSourceMQTT, code)`. The suppression itself is asserted by the wave's own test internal/alarm/codes/codes_test.go TestFacadeMatchDuressBoundsProbeWorkPerSource (`probe budget exhausted: want no verification work until the window elapses`) — what is missing is that a correct non-duress PIN counts toward that budget. Note by contrast Validate clears the code-plane ledger on any correct code (facade.go:202 `f.limiter.recordSuccess(source)`).
confirmed.verifier_reason: Reproduced with a temporary test in internal/alarm/codes (since deleted): a facade holding a duress code '9999' and an ordinary PIN '1234' suppresses the real duress match from source 'mqtt' after five MatchDuress calls carrying the correct ordinary PIN — the test asserting no suppression failed. Mechanism as claimed: only c.duress rows enter duressCandidates (facade.go:232-238), so a valid non-duress PIN falls through to f.probes.recordFailure (:260-262); recordSuccess only fires on a duress match, ratelimit.go has no decay, and the allow() gate at :246-251 returns before any verification during the lockout, so no journal row and no AlarmDuressEvent is produced. Production path is real: mqtt sink -> DisarmWithCode(ctx, zoneID, "", "mqtt", code) (daemon_north.go:498-501), engine.go:702-706 calls matchDuress on the already-disarmed branch, and IsOperatorSource (engine.go:76-83) does not cover 'mqtt', so limited=true. Note the pre-existing accepted design: five WRONG codes already mute duress for 60s (codes_test.go:480-505) — the new element is that a correct PIN also spends the budget. Kept at medium: it needs five code-carrying disarms of an already-disarmed zone to line up with a coercion event, and the lockout starts at 60s.

plausible.title: The SPA's simple-schedule save drops `domain`, so the lock encoding never runs on any write from the UI
plausible.claim: The editor reads schedule.domain (SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:30-40) and renders the domain-specific widgets from it, including the lock mode / lock action / permission pickers (:379-466). But save() rebuilds the PUT body from scratch as `{ channel, kind: "simple", simple_entries }` (:200-204) and omits `domain`, which hmapi.ClimateSchedule declares as `json:"domain,omitempty"` (pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:266). PutClimateSchedule therefore passes sched.Domain == "" into serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain, whose only branch is `if domain == "lock"` — so applyLockEncoding is skipped for every save originating in the SPA. This is independent of finding C21-schedules-1: fixing the read-side domain mapping alone would still leave every SPA write unencoded.
plausible.failure_scenario: On a lock device whose domain resolved correctly, the operator picks lock_action = "unlock_autorelock_end" in the SPA and saves. The PUT body carries lock_action but no domain, so serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain (schedules.go:796-809) takes the non-lock path; applyLockEncoding never converts lock_action into (LEVEL 1.0, DURATION_BASE 7, DURATION_FACTOR 31). simpleScheduleToDomain (schedules.go:772-786) does not copy LockMode/LockAction/Permission into schedule.SimpleEntry either, so the fields are dropped entirely and the slot is written with whatever raw level the DTO happened to carry. The chosen lock action silently does not reach the device.
plausible.evidence: assets/ui/src/lib/components/schedule/SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:200-205 `const payload: ClimateSchedule = { channel: schedule.channel, kind: "simple", simple_entries: entries }; await api.putDeviceSchedule(address, payload);` — no `domain` key. internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:919 `serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain(sched.SimpleEntries, sched.Domain, ...)`; :799 `if domain == "lock"`. internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:772-786 simpleScheduleToDomain copies Weekdays/Time/Condition/AstroType/AstroOffsetMinutes/TargetChannels/Level/Level2/Duration/RampTime/Color*/OutputBehaviour but not LockMode/LockAction/Permission. pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:266 `Domain string \`json:"domain,omitempty"\``.
plausible.verifier_reason: Every code fact checks out, but the user-visible failure is currently unreachable, so this is a latent half-fix rather than a live defect. Verified: SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:199-205 builds `{channel, kind:"simple", simple_entries}` with no `domain` key; the daemon has NO fallback — PutClimateSchedule (schedules.go:919) passes `sched.Domain` straight into serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain, whose only branch is `if domain == "lock"` (:799), and nothing re-infers the domain on the write path (detectScheduleDomain is called only from the READ path, GetClimateSchedule:446). simpleScheduleToDomain (:772-786) really does drop LockMode/LockAction/Permission. A temporary in-package test confirmed the divergence directly: same entry, domain="" serialises to LEVEL=0 with no DURATION_BASE/FACTOR; domain="lock" serialises to LEVEL=1, DURATION_BASE=7, DURATION_FACTOR=31, TARGET_CHANNELS=1. So the mechanism is exactly as claimed. What does not close is reachability. The SPA only renders the lock picker under `{:else if domain === "lock"}` (:379), and no device in the fleet ever yields that domain: detectScheduleDomain matches the *_WEEK_PROFILE channel FIRST (schedules.go:481-492), and every lock in godevccu's 399-device fleet carries SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE as its week-profile channel (HmIP-DLD ch10, HmIP-DLP ch10; KEYMATIC devices have no week-profile channel at all). domainFromWeekProfileType("SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE") returns "switch", so the operator gets the switch widget and can never pick a lock_action to lose. The lock branch is dead UI today. Two guards the claimant did not mention, neither of which rescues it: CopySchedule/CopyClimateProfile round-trip the DTO from GetClimateSchedule, so they DO carry `domain`; and a REST/WS/MCP client that sends domain:"lock" explicitly gets correct encoding. Not fixed on origin/main (d281e2e2 touches only daemon jobs/version). Severity re-rated medium->low: no observable consequence until the read-side domain detection is corrected, at which point it becomes real.
plausible.verifier_evidence: assets/ui/src/lib/components/schedule/SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:199-205 (payload without `domain`; the lock widget's own comment at :381-383 claims "level/duration/target_channels are recomputed by the backend on save" — that recomputation is gated on the field the SPA omits). internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:919, :796-809, :811-838, :740-789, :446. plausible.title: rega.EscapeString does not escape CR/LF, so a multi-line string-sysvar value breaks set_system_variable.fn's `!#` header comment open and lands in the script as source text
plausible.claim: substitute (runner.go:495-515) runs placeholderPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc over the WHOLE script body, including the `!# ...` header comments, and the only escaping applied is EscapeString (runner.go:520-524), which replaces `\` and `"` and nothing else. `!#` is a line comment in ReGa (every script and every occu WebUI .fn repeats it per line), so a substituted value containing LF/CR terminates the comment early and the remainder of the value lands in the script as source text. set_system_variable.fn interpolates the operator's value twice: once inside a comment — line 2 `!# Params: ##name## (string), ##value## (string)` — and once inside a double-quoted literal, line 10 `string sValue = "##value##";`. The value arrives verbatim from any north-bound plane: internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:827-834 stringToWire returns v.String unchanged, Sysvar.Set (:550) hands it to hubJSONRPCWriter.SetSysvar (hub_wiring.go:2002-2010) which passes it straight into rega.Run. No layer strips or rejects control characters (contrast the ReGa parameter that IS guarded: internal/auth/ccuauth/store.go:41 usernamePattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,64}$`, whose comment states the rule — 'bounds the username to the CCU's legal character set before it is interpolated into the user-level ReGa script ... defence against ReGa injection').
plausible.failure_scenario: An operator (role 'operator', no script privileges of its own — the daemon exposes no raw ReGa endpoint) writes a string sysvar via PUT /api/v1/hub/sysvars/{name}, the WS set_sysvar command, or the MQTT command plane, with a value containing a newline, e.g. "line1\ndom.GetObject(ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES).Get(\"Alarmzone\").State(true); !#". After substitution the script's line 2 ends at `line1` and the injected text becomes a top-level statement executed on the CCU under the daemon's privileged service session. Even in the benign reading the script no longer has the shape it was written with: the header comment is closed early and the payload is re-parsed as source, so an ordinary multi-line note value cannot be stored (Run returns empty output, SetSysvar reports 'rega write declined'). Only the escaping of `\` and `"` was designed for; the newline case was not considered anywhere on the path.
plausible.evidence: internal/client/rega/runner.go:497-505 `out := placeholderPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc(body, func(match string) string { ... return EscapeString(v) })` (applied to the whole body, comments included); :520-524 `func EscapeString(v string) string { v = strings.ReplaceAll(v, \`\\\`, ...); v = strings.ReplaceAll(v, \`\"\`, ...); return v }`. internal/client/rega/scripts/set_system_variable.fn:2 `!# Params: ##name## (string), ##value## (string)`; :10 `string sValue = "##value##";`. Path: internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:550 + :827-834; internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:2007-2010. The guarded counterpart proving the project treats this as an injection surface: internal/auth/ccuauth/store.go:38-41 and internal/client/rega/scripts/get_user_level.fn:2-4.
plausible.verifier_reason: The daemon-side half is proven. A throw-away test in package rega (deleted) ran the real loadScript(RegaScriptSetSystemVariable) + substitute() with value "line1\ndom.GetObject(...).State(true);\n!#" and produced a script whose line 2 comment ends at `line1`, with the remainder sitting at top level, and whose line 10 string literal is left unterminated across three lines. Reachability to the wire is closed: PUT /api/v1/hub/sysvars/{name} (router.go:1246, operator role) -> hmtypes.NewParamValue (no control-char rejection) -> Sysvar.Set -> stringToWire returns v.String unchanged -> hubJSONRPCWriter.SetSysvar (hub_wiring.go:2002-2010) routes STRING values through rega.Run -> Runner.Run:76 substitute, :88 Call - no sanitiser anywhere. The claimed guarded counterpart is real (ccuauth/store.go:38-41 usernamePattern, and ADR 0043:199 names ReGa injection as the threat). WHAT IS MISSING for CONFIRMED: the CCU's own ReGa parser semantics. Whether the injected top-level statement executes, or the unterminated literal on line 10 aborts the whole script at parse time, can only be settled against a live CCU, and that is a write I am not authorised to make. plausible.title: Coalescer publishes the result before dropping the map entry, so the purge invariant holds only eventually (racy committed assertion; no operator-visible effect)
plausible.claim: The rewrite split what used to be one critical section into two steps performed by two goroutines. run() calls call.settle(v, err) at coalesce.go:209, which closes call.done (coalesce.go:98) and releases every awaiter immediately; only afterwards does run() take c.mu and delete the entry (coalesce.go:211-216). await() returns to its caller as soon as call.done is closed (coalesce.go:241-243). There is therefore a guaranteed window in which every Do for a key has already returned while c.calls[key] still holds the settled call. Before the wave the two were atomic: the old leader did `close(call.done); delete(c.calls, key)` inside the same c.mu section before returning, so no caller could observe the result while the entry still existed. Consequences: (a) InFlight()/Stats().InFlight (coalesce.go:290-307) report a call in flight when none is; (b) Do's admission test is `ok && call.active > 0` (coalesce.go:162) and active only drops when each participant runs leave(), so while participants of a finished group are still waking up, a brand-new caller joins the already-settled call and is handed its result with fn never running for it — Do's own contract at coalesce.go:144 says 'Completed calls are purged so a later invocation starts a fresh run'.
plausible.failure_scenario: Observed, not inferred: `go test -race -count=2 ./internal/client/reliability/ ./internal/client/ ./internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/` on f356cb40 fails with `--- FAIL: TestCoalescerEvictionStress1000GoroutinesMultiKey (0.38s) coalesce_eviction_test.go:102: InFlight after drain=1, want 0 (calls map leaked entries)`. The committed test fans out 1000 goroutines over 100 keys, waits for every Do to return, and asserts the map is empty — the invariant the old code held structurally and the new code only holds eventually. It passes in isolation and fails under machine load, i.e. it is a new intermittent CI failure. On the production path (InterfaceClient.Call with a setValue coalesce key, interface_client.go:477) the same window means a caller arriving microseconds after an identical write completed is attached to that finished call, gets RequestCoalescedEvent + a success return, and issues no wire call of its own.
plausible.evidence: internal/client/reliability/coalesce.go:206-221 `func (c *Coalescer) run(...) { defer call.cancel(); v, err := invokeCoalesced(ctx, fn); call.settle(v, err); c.mu.Lock(); if cur, ok := c.calls[key]; ok && cur == call { delete(c.calls, key) } ... }` — settle precedes the lock; coalesce.go:90-99 `settle` closes call.done; coalesce.go:239-248 `await` returns on `<-call.done` before run's delete can have run; coalesce.go:162 `if call, ok := c.calls[key]; ok && call.active > 0`. What does NOT hold is the impact. (1) The claimed reproducer failed to reproduce: `go test -race -count=2 ./internal/client/reliability/ ./internal/client/ ./internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/` passed, as did 120 consecutive -race runs of TestCoalescerEvictionStress1000GoroutinesMultiKey under a full-core busy load - so 'new intermittent CI failure' is unquantified, not observed here. (2) Coalescer.InFlight()/Stats() have NO production consumer (grep over internal/, cmd/, pkg/ finds only the doc comment 'Intended for metrics and tests'), so the overcount is test-only. (3) The 'later caller joins a finished call' half is a microsecond-wide extension of a deliberate behaviour: coalesceKeyFor (backend_caller.go:85-98) keys on (priority,address,parameter,TYPE,value), and its own doc says 'a burst of redundant repeats ... is deduplicated into one wire call' - so the folded call is a byte-identical repeat, not a lost write. refuted.title: Five write handlers decode request bodies without their own MaxBytesReader (the 1 MiB ceiling is applied by outer middleware)

Its own doc comment states this is deliberately mirroring handlers' maxRequestBodyBytes because it 'runs ahead of every handler'. Reachability of the bypass is closed off in a shipped deployment: OpenAPIValidate defaults to TRUE when unset, FailOpen is hard-coded false, and all five cited paths are declared in assets/openapi.yaml (so FindRoute matches rather than skipping) - /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/flags:450, /groups:584, /system/ccu/{central}/position:1776, /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/master-profiles/match:3377, /matter/factory-reset:5890. Residual defence-in-depth gap only: if an operator sets openapi_validate: false or the spec file is missing, buildOpenAPIValidator returns nil and these five lose the ceiling while every DecodeJSON handler keeps it - worth tidying, but not the claimed unbounded allocation.

The same file also breaks the repo-wide SHA-pinning convention: its own `changes` job (line 32) and essentially every job in ci.yml/e2e.yml/nightly.yml/etc. pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA with a version comment (e.g. `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1`), but spa-e2e.yml's `run` job (the one that actually executes `npm ci` and `npx playwright test` inside a third-party container) uses floating tags: `actions/checkout@v7.0.1` (line 65), `actions/setup-node@v7.0.0` (line 66), `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (line 77). The same unpinned-tag lapse also exists (lower risk, since those trigger on schedule/push-to-main or pull_request with only setup-python) in docs.yml, cross-stack-parity.yml, integration.yml, model-parity.yml and chiptool.yml, showing the SHA-pinning hardening was applied inconsistently across the workflow set.
refuted.failure_scenario: spa-e2e.yml triggers on `pull_request:` with no `types:` restriction (so it runs on every PR, including from forks, that touches assets/ui/**). If actions/checkout@v7, actions/setup-node@v7 or actions/upload-artifact@v7's tag were ever repointed (upstream compromise, or GitHub Actions cache poisoning of a mutable tag) the `run` job would execute that code with whatever permissions the token defaults to for this repo — a wider blast radius than every other workflow, which the project's own convention (SHA pin + explicit `contents: read`) exists specifically to close off. This is the same class of gap CLAUDE.md's git-workflow guidance treats seriously for the codebase's other hardening layers.

Swap rebuilt the bridge from scratch, so its Discovery cache and per-DP slot state are empty ... refuted.title: The wiring guard's shape filter excludes data setters by documented design; no live collaborator seam was shown escaping it
refuted.claim: injectsCollaborator (line 243) admits a method into the walk only when it is non-variadic, returns nothing-or-self, and every parameter is either a single 'collaborator' or a Basic scoping key. isCollaborator (line 288) recognises exactly three shapes: pointer-to-named, signature, named-interface/named-func. A collaborator handed over as a SLICE, a MAP, or a pointer-to-basic is none of those and falls into the `default: return false` of the parameter loop, so the whole method is dropped; so is any seam that returns an error (returnsNothingOrSelf, line 323) or is variadic (line 245). I enumerated the module through go/packages with the guard's own predicates: 57 exported Set*/Attach*/Register* methods are excluded by these clauses AND have no production caller — i.e. they are outside the guard entirely, neither flagged nor ratcheted. Most are ordinary data setters, but a real subset is collaborator/state injection that only tests call — the exact state the guard's own header calls a defect ('a seam kept for tests belongs deleted, because a setter only tests call is a setter production does not need'): store/visibility.ModelValidator.SetRelevantMasterPrefixes([]string) and .SetRelevantMasterChannels(map[string]map[int]struct{}), model/device.Channel.SetLinkPeerSourceCategories/TargetCategories([]string), model/generic.DataPoint.SetStatusParameter(string,[]string), model/custom/textdisplay.TextDisplay.SetAvailableIntervals([]string), matter/cluster/core.Descriptor.SetPartsList([]uint16). One is called by nothing at all, production or test: model/weekprofile.ProfileDataPoint.SetSupportedScheduleFields([]hmenum.ScheduleField) — and its own doc claims a caller that does not exist. A secondary, currently latent hole in the same guard: findCalledFuncs -> receiverInterface (line 439) requires the receiver to be a *types.Named, and funcKey (line 454) returns "" for an unnamed receiver, so a wiring call dispatched through an ANONYMOUS interface literal is dropped from the 'called' set entirely; production uses that idiom (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1893-1896 calls sp.SetStatusParameter through an inline `interface{ SetStatusParameter(...) }`). No seam currently inside the walk is wired only that way, so today it would misfire rather than miss — but the standard remedy for a misfire is a ratchet entry, which would then permanently exempt a live seam with a false reason.
refuted.failure_scenario: Give a collaborator-injection seam a slice/map parameter or an error return — the two most natural variants of the shape — and it leaves the guard's field of view without any test failing, without an entry in wiringSettersWithoutCaller, and without appearing in the guard's 'stale entry' report. Concretely today: model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:365 documents 'SetSupportedScheduleFields ... Called by the pipeline once the MASTER paramset is available', and the field doc at line 166 says 'Nil until the pipeline populates it'. The pipeline never calls it (grep over the whole repo returns only the definition and the doc references); ProfileDataPoint.SupportedScheduleFields() (line 358) therefore returns nil for every device forever, and it too has no reader. The extraction the pair was built for runs elsewhere (internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:925,944 call weekprofile.ExtractSupportedScheduleFields directly), so the operator sees no symptom — but the guard that exists to make exactly this silence loud never looked at it, and the comment naming the pipeline as its caller is refuted.

Refuted-caller symbol: internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:365-372 (setter), :358-363 (reader), :166-168 (field doc 'Nil until the pipeline populates it'); production extraction that bypasses both: internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:925 `supported := weekprofile.ExtractSupportedScheduleFields(descKeys)`. refuted.title: Whole-list-replace write semantics are a divergence already recorded in by_design.md; the chunked-ACL failure is unproven
refuted.claim: The path decoders store ListIndex (im/read.go:239-241 and im/path.go:133-135, both `p.ListIndex = uint16(el.Uint & 0xFFFF); p.HasListIndex = true`) — and set HasListIndex=true for a TLV Null element too, since el.IsNull is not consulted, so 'append' and 'index 0' become indistinguishable. HandleWriteRequest (im/write.go:239-361) then never reads HasListIndex: it validates only HasCluster/HasAttribute (:273) and dispatches `d.Write(ctx, w.Path, w.Value)` (:331). matter.js implements the three-way semantics explicitly in AttributeWriteResponse.ts:412-443 — listIndex absent = REPLACE_ALL, listIndex === null = ADD (push one element onto the existing list), a concrete numeric listIndex = StatusResponseError(Status.InvalidAction) — and InteractionServer.ts:447-449 additionally tracks `previousProcessedAttributePath` so a list ADD without a prior REPLACE_ALL to the same attribute is answered BUSY. connectedhomeip's WriteClient always emits this shape: WriteClient.h:243-275 encodes a non-ACL list attribute as an (empty) ReplaceAll AttributeDataIB followed by one AppendItem AttributeDataIB per element with `path.mListOp = AppendItem` (ListIndex = Null), with AccessControl the documented exception that packs entries into the ReplaceAll and appends only the remainder.
refuted.failure_scenario: AccessControl.ACL is the one list attribute loom can decode, and an entry set that does not fit one AttributeDataIB arrives as ReplaceAll + AppendItem IBs whose Data is a single AccessControlEntryStruct (TLV Structure, not Array). decodeACLList rejects that at attribute_value_reader.go:41-43 (`AccessControl.ACL: value is not array (type=0x15)`); the error propagates out of readAttributeData -> UnmarshalWriteRequestTLV, and bridge/receive.go:406-410 returns the error without sending any WriteResponse at all. The controller sees no answer, MRP-retransmits the whole write, and the ACL update times out. Independently, a write carrying a concrete numeric ListIndex is silently applied as a whole-attribute replace instead of being rejected with InvalidAction.
refuted.evidence: internal/north/matter/im/write.go:264-361 (HandleWriteRequest body — grep for HasListIndex returns no hit in the file); internal/north/matter/im/read.go:239-241; internal/north/matter/im/path.go:133-135. Decode rejection: internal/north/matter/bridge/attribute_value_reader.go:40-43. No-response path: internal/north/matter/bridge/receive.go:406-410 `req, err := im.UnmarshalWriteRequestTLV(dec, attributeValueReader); if err != nil { b.logger.Warn(...); return err }`. Gold standard: ../matter.js/packages/protocol/src/action/server/AttributeWriteResponse.ts:412-443; ../matter.js/packages/node/src/node/server/InteractionServer.ts:447-449. Wire truth: ../connectedhomeip/src/app/WriteClient.h:243-275 and the documented WriteRequestMessage shape at :596-600 (`ListIndex = Null`). Not in notes/parity/by_design.md.
refuted.verifier_reason: The code reads as claimed — im/read.go:239-241 and im/path.go:133-135 set HasListIndex without consulting el.IsNull, and HandleWriteRequest (write.go:239-361) never looks at it — and matter.js does implement the three-way semantics (AttributeWriteResponse.ts writeValue: numeric listIndex -> StatusResponseError(InvalidAction), undefined -> REPLACE_ALL, null -> ADD/push), which I read in ../matter.js myself. But the claim's key evidentiary assertion, 'Not in notes/parity/by_design.md', is false: BD-chip-P2-D-L4-NEW-1 (notes/parity/by_design.md:2193-2199) records exactly this divergence — 'OpenCCU-Loom's write dispatcher treats every list write as a whole-list replace ... The spec's ListIndex partial-append path is a chip-tool-specific test-suite path that no production controller uses' — so it is a deliberate, documented decision, not drift. The failure scenario is also not closed: connectedhomeip WriteClient.h:243-266 emits AppendItem IBs for ACL only when the entry set does not fit one AttributeDataIB (`VerifyOrReturnError(chunkingNeeded, CHIP_NO_ERROR)` returns early otherwise), so the common Apple/Google/chip-tool ACL write stays a single array that decodeACLList accepts; no evidence was given that a supported controller ever chunks. The residual — the by_design rationale says 'full list in a single WriteRequest' without acknowledging chip's chunking threshold, and a numeric ListIndex is silently applied as a replace instead of InvalidAction — is worth a by_design refinement at low severity, not a defect.

refuted.title: Dimmable-light CurrentLevel write asserts uint8, but CurrentLevel is a read-only attribute and dimming never goes through MatterWrite
refuted.claim: lightLevelServer.MatterWrite for LevelControl.CurrentLevel still does a bare `value.(uint8)` type assertion. The IM write layer decodes every unsigned TLV integer to uint64 (documented at internal/north/matter/cluster/coerce.go:6-12, and fixed for the exact same class of bug in internal/model/generic/switch_matter.go:356-378 and internal/model/custom/switch/matter.go:421-443 in this same PR wave), so the assertion never matches a real controller's write.
refuted.failure_scenario: Any Matter controller (Apple Home, Google Home, HA) dims a bridged HmIP dimmer/light via LevelControl.CurrentLevel. attribute_value_reader.go decodes the TLV uint8 to Go uint64; lightLevelServer.MatterWrite (light/matter.go:519) fails the `value.(uint8)` assertion, returns errMatterValueType, and the write reports IM StatusFailure. Brightness control never works on any dimmable Matter-bridged light — only through on/off remains functional.
refuted.evidence: light/matter.go:515-528 `func (s lightLevelServer) MatterWrite(...) { ... b, ok := value.(uint8); if !ok { return fmt.Errorf(...) } ... }`, no cluster.AsUint8/matterWriteUint8-style coercion. Wired for every dimmable light: light/matter.go:169-172 `if l.Capabilities.Dimmable { return []interfaces.MatterClusterServer{lightOnOffServer{l: l}, lightLevelServer{l: l}, ...} }`. Sibling fix pattern: internal/north/matter/cluster/coerce.go:47-53 AsUint8, internal/model/custom/switch/matter.go:434-443 matterWriteUint8, internal/model/generic/switch_matter.go:369-378 matterGenericWriteUint8 — none of these three helpers is used in light/matter.go.
refuted.verifier_reason: The assertion exists as quoted (light/matter.go:519, unchanged on origin/main) and the decoder does yield uint64 (attribute_value_reader.go:238-242). The failure scenario does not hold. LevelControl.CurrentLevel is `access: "R V"` — read-only — in matter.js's generated schema (packages/model/src/standard/elements/level-control.element.ts:30-33), so no controller dims by writing it; Apple/Google/HA all send MoveToLevel / MoveToLevelWithOnOff, which the bridge decodes straight into a wire.MoveToLevelRequest (bridge/fields_reader.go:62, :94) and dispatches through MatterInvoke -> extractMoveToLevel's `case wire.MoveToLevelRequest` (light/matter.go:530-545, :765-767). Brightness control therefore works; nothing on the production write path (endpoint/dispatcher.go:569 writeOne is the only .MatterWrite call site) ever carries CurrentLevel from a conformant controller. The cited siblings are not the same case: matterWriteUint8/16 are used for OnTime, OffWaitTime and StartUpOnOff (switch/matter.go:259-285, generic/switch_matter.go:222-240), all genuinely RW — and light/matter.go already uses matterWriteUint16/matterWriteUint8 for exactly those three attributes on lightOnOffServer (:285-311). Residual nit only: a non-conformant write of the read-only CurrentLevel returns StatusFailure where matter.js would answer UnsupportedWrite; accepting the write at all is the larger divergence, so coercing the type would be the wrong fix.
refuted.verifier_evidence: internal/model/custom/light/matter.go:515-528 (assertion), :285-311 (coercion already used for the RW attributes), :530-545 + :764-783 (command path); internal/north/matter/bridge/fields_reader.go:62,94; internal/north/matter/endpoint/dispatcher.go:562-573; ../matter.js/packages/model/src/standard/elements/level-control.element.ts:30-33 `Attribute({ name: "CurrentLevel", id: 0x0, type: "uint8", access: "R V", ... })`

unverified_low.title: The climate write path's unsupported-field filter is a permanent no-op, and its comment claims an effect the code cannot have
unverified_low.claim: In the `case "climate", ""` branch of PutClimateSchedule the raw paramset is passed through ExtractSupportedScheduleFields + FilterRawScheduleByFields with a comment saying it filters ENDTIME_*/TEMPERATURE_* keys the device does not expose. A climate paramset contains only `P<n>_ENDTIME_<DAY>_<slot>` / `P<n>_TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_<slot>` or their bare forms, none of which contain "_WP_", so `supported` is always nil and FilterRawScheduleByFields returns raw unchanged on its `len(supported) == 0` guard. A reader auditing the write path is told the guard exists.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:938-946 — the comment at :939-943 followed by `supported := weekprofile.ExtractSupportedScheduleFields(descKeys); raw = weekprofile.FilterRawScheduleByFields(raw, supported)`. internal/model/weekprofile/channel_keys.go:104 `const scheduleKeyPrefix = "_WP_"`, :122-130 `before, after, ok := strings.Cut(key, scheduleKeyPrefix); if !ok { continue }; if !allDigits(prefix) || prefix == "" { continue }`, :156-158 `if len(seen) == 0 { return nil }`; :205 `if len(supported) == 0 || len(raw) == 0 { return raw }`. The contradiction is stated in the same function at internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:931: "the field filter below does not catch it (ExtractSupportedScheduleFields only recognises WP_ keys)".

unverified_low.title: MQTT renders an absent schedule duration as "0ms", the daemon's own encoding for a real zero duration
unverified_low.claim: simpleEntryJSON rewrites an empty Duration/RampTime to the literal "0ms" before publishing. In this codebase "" and "0ms" are two different values: weekprofile.ZeroDuration == "0ms" is documented as the genuine (base 0, factor 0) pair the CCU stores, while "" means "no duration — leave the device's value alone". decodeWireDuration returns "" both for factor 0 and for any factor above MaxTimeBaseFactor, which includes the firmware's "permanent" sentinel (base 7, factor 31) that the lock domain uses for auto-relock-end / unlock / standing permission. The MQTT plane therefore reports "permanent" as "0ms", the opposite duration.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: A door-lock slot whose wire pair is (DURATION_BASE 7, DURATION_FACTOR 31) — schedule.LockActionTable's encoding for lock_autorelock_end / unlock_autorelock_end / autorelock_end — decodes to Duration "" and is published on the Zeitplan attributes topic as `"duration": "0ms"`. A consumer reading the attribute sees a slot that reverts immediately where the device holds the state until further notice.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2932-2937 `if duration == "" { duration = "0ms" }` / `if rampTime == "" { rampTime = "0ms" }`. internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:984-994 `// ZeroDuration is the string form of the (base 0, factor 0) pair — a duration of zero ... It exists because "" already means "leave the device's duration alone"` / `const ZeroDuration = "0ms"`. internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:699-704 decodeWireDuration returns "" for `factor <= 0 || factor > MaxTimeBaseFactor` (MaxTimeBaseFactor = 30, :936). internal/model/schedule/lock.go:31-33 encodes LockActionAutoRelockEnd/Unlock/Open as durBase 7, durFactor 31.

unverified_low.title: Program.EnabledDefault is rewritten by the periodic hub refresh with no lock while REST reads it through an equally unguarded accessor
unverified_low.claim: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:979 `existing.EnabledDefault = hubEnabledDefault(p.IsInternal, meta.description, opts.programMarkers)` writes a promoted field of a live `*hub.Program` directly, outside any lock — while the sibling sysvar upsert 217 lines below routes the identical field through the guarded whole-descriptor write (internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1196 `existing.ApplyMeta(hub.SysvarMeta{ ... EnabledDefault: ..., ... })`, which takes s.mu). The read side matches: `Sysvar` deliberately shadows the accessor so the field is read under the same lock — internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:427-431 `func (s *Sysvar) EnabledByDefault() bool { s.mu.RLock(); defer s.mu.RUnlock(); return s.HubDataPoint.EnabledByDefault() }`, documented at :422-426 as existing 'so the EnabledDefault field — which the hub refresh rewrites through [ApplyMeta] under s.mu — is read under the same lock'. `Program` has no such shadow, so a program read falls through to internal/model/hub/generic_data_point.go:172-179 `func (h *HubDataPoint) EnabledByDefault() bool { ... return h.EnabledDefault }` — an unsynchronised field read. Both sides of the program path are therefore unsynchronised; the fix that closed this for sysvars was not applied to programs. Contrast: the program path DID get the guarded treatment for its other refreshed fields — internal/model/hub/program.go:264-273 `UpdateMetadata` routes Name through `p.SetName(name)` and IsInternal through `p.mu`.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: Steady-state daemon with at least one CCU program. The scheduler's program-refresh job (wired at internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:410-419 `Programs: gated(func(ctx) error { loadPrograms(ctx, jc, runner, unit.HubModel, writer, scanOpts) ... })`) runs `loadPrograms` on a scheduler worker goroutine and rewrites `existing.EnabledDefault` on every pass (hub_wiring.go:979). Concurrently an operator's `GET /programs` request builds its DTO on an HTTP handler goroutine at internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:433 `e.EnabledDefault = p.EnabledByDefault()`, which reads the same field with no lock. The two accesses have no happens-before edge: a -race build flags it, and the response can report the pre-refresh enabled-by-default flag for a program whose markers just changed, so a program the operator just marked shows up with `enabled_default:false` until the next poll.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:978-979 — `existing.UpdateMetadata(p.Name, p.IsInternal, writer)` / `existing.EnabledDefault = hubEnabledDefault(p.IsInternal, meta.description, opts.programMarkers)` (the first call is guarded, the second is a bare field write on the same pointer). Enclosing function: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:927 `func loadPrograms(ctx context.Context, jc *jsonrpc.Client, runner *rega.Runner, h *hub.Hub, writer hub.ProgramWriter, opts hubScanOptions) error`, invoked from the periodic refresh hook at internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:412 and from the boot scan at :280. Read side: internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:433 `e.EnabledDefault = p.EnabledByDefault()` -> internal/model/hub/generic_data_point.go:172-179 (no lock). Sibling that IS fixed: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1196 `existing.ApplyMeta(hub.SysvarMeta{...})` + internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:404-420 + internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:422-431. Checked and excluded: `Program.Description` is read raw at internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:419 but is never rewritten after construction (internal/model/hub/program.go:264-273 UpdateMetadata does not touch it), so that read is safe.

unverified_low.claim: c706d9d7 added `if (err.status === 423) return t("api.error.locked")` to friendlyError. The daemon returns 423 from three different causes: the channel control-lock (`internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:852` writeChannelLocked), a missing/lapsed MASTER edit token (`internal/north/rest/handlers/paramsets.go:44` enforceEditLock) and an already-held edit session (`internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:173`). The new branch answers all three with the control-lock text and discards the daemon's problem.detail, which previously reached the operator through the generic 4xx frame at client.ts:2537-2539. The branch's own comment asserts 'Surfaces that need the lock *holder* (the edit-session banner) branch on 423 before reaching here' — ChannelPanel.svelte does (lines 352, 594, 829), but SecureTransmission.svelte does not, so the fix is applied at one call site and not its sibling.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: Operator opens a channel's MASTER panel, leaves it idle past the 5-min edit-lock TTL (or mounts SecureTransmission without a token — the component's own prop doc says 'Omitting it on a gated mount yields 423 on the write'), then flips the 'secure transmission' switch. `api.putParamset(addr, "MASTER", {AES_ACTIVE}, editToken)` answers 423 with detail 'hold an edit session (<key>) and present its token via X-Edit-Token'. SecureTransmission.svelte:95-98 toasts `friendlyError(err, t)`, which now reads 'Locked — this channel is protected against control writes. Lift the lock in the channel's flags.' The operator is sent to the channel flags editor, where nothing is locked; the real fix (re-open the edit session / reload the panel) is never named, and the daemon's detail that named it is dropped. Before this wave the same failure read 'Request rejected (423) — hold an edit session ... via X-Edit-Token'.
unverified_low.evidence: assets/ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:2513-2519 `if (err.status === 423) { // A control write against a locked channel. ... Surfaces that need the lock *holder* (the edit-session banner) branch on 423 before reaching here. return t("api.error.locked"); }`; assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:3178 `"api.error.locked": "Locked — this channel is protected against control writes. Lift the lock in the channel's flags."`; assets/ui/src/lib/components/channel/SecureTransmission.svelte:10-14 `// Omitting it on a gated mount yields 423 on the write.` and :82-98 `await api.putParamset(channelAddress, "MASTER", { AES_ACTIVE: next }, editToken); ... } catch (err) { toastStore.error(t("channel.secure_transmission.failed"), friendlyError(err, t)); }` — no 423 branch, unlike the sibling ChannelPanel.svelte:594 `if (err instanceof ApiError && err.status === 423) { lockSession = null; toastStore.error(t("channel.save_failed"), t("channel.lock_lost")); }`; internal/north/rest/handlers/paramsets.go:44-47 `problem.Write(w, http.StatusLocked, problem.New(problem.TypeConflict, r, "Edit lock required", "hold an edit session ("+lockKey+") and present its token via "+EditTokenHeader))` vs internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:852-855 `"the channel is locked against control writes; lift the lock via PUT /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/flags"`. Side note in the same hunk: the fall-through comment at client.ts:2532 still enumerates 423 (`// Everything else (400 / 409 / 422 / 423 …)`) although that status can no longer reach it.

unverified_low.title: A walk-test session survives an arm, then silently swallows every activation of the zone after the next disarm
unverified_low.claim: a.walk is cleared only by WalkTestStop. Arm/beginArm/completeArm, disarmLocked, finishTriggered, Reload and reloadSensorsLocked never touch it, and Arm does not refuse a zone with a running session. A walk test started on a disarmed zone therefore stays open across arming, the whole armed period and the disarm, and while the zone is disarmed again HandleSensorEvent hands every member activation to the (stale) walk consumer and returns before the disarmed-state handling.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: A technician starts a walk test on zone `eg` (REST POST .../walktest/start; the zone must be disarmed). Before stopping it, the zone's AutoArm schedule fires — or anyone arms via HA/SPA/keypad. The arm is accepted, the session stays open, and every sensor the technician now trips triggers a real alarm. After the incident's post-trigger disarm the session is still open, so from then on: the door chime never sounds (engine.go:925-927 is unreachable), and a pending auto-rearm is never deferred by member activity (engine.go:921-924), i.e. the zone re-arms on schedule while people are moving through it. The walk-test badge stays lit on every surface until someone happens to press Stop.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/alarm/engine/walktest.go:58-61 (start; only guard is state==disarmed and walk==nil) and :91 `a.walk = nil` in WalkTestStop — `grep -rn "\.walk\b" --include=*.go internal/alarm/ | grep -v _test.go` returns hits in walktest.go only, so no other production path clears it. internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:420-454 Arm and :460-556 beginArm contain no walk check; internal/alarm/reload.go:202-223 disarmLocked does not clear it either. The swallow: internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:895-898 `if e.walkTestObserve(ctx, a, sensorID, active) && a.state == hmenum.AlarmZoneStateDisarmed { return }` placed before the disarmed-state block at :921-928 (auto-rearm defer + chime), with walktest.go:134-140 returning true for any activation while walk != nil and the zone is disarmed.

unverified_low.title: Under an implausible clock a restored silenced incident skips the S3 counter-stop, so a physically sounding siren stays on
unverified_low.claim: restoreTriggered handles the implausible-clock case in a branch that returns before the `inc.Silenced` block, so the counter-stop StopAll that the silenced branch performs — explicitly documented as covering a crash that landed between the silence persist and the output stop — is not issued on that path. The plausible-clock sibling issues it; the implausible one does not.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: An RTC-less host (the case clockPlausible exists for: daemon starts before NTP sync, timers.go:64-78) crashes after the operator silenced a triggered zone but before Manager.StopAll reached the siren. On restore, clockPlausible is false, restoreTriggered reschedules the trigger timer, journals `triggered_restored_implausible_clock` and returns at :445 — no StopAll. The siren keeps sounding until the full trigger duration elapses and onTriggerElapsed -> finishTriggered finally stops it (up to MaxTriggerSeconds = 600 s), instead of being stopped at boot.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/alarm/engine/restore.go:433-446 `if !plausible { ... e.scheduleStateTimer(a, timerKindTrigger, remaining); e.persist(ctx, a); e.journalEntry(... "triggered_restored_implausible_clock" ...); return }` — the early return. The sibling that does issue it is :465-477 `if inc.Silenced { // S3 persistence: a silenced incident never sounds again. The counter-stop covers a crash that landed between the silence persist and the output stop — stopping again is free. if err := e.outputs.StopAll(ctx, a.id, inc.ID); ... }`, reachable only after the plausible-clock path. The eventual stop is internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:1240 `if inc != nil && !inc.Silenced && ...` -> :1268 finishTriggered -> :1280 StopAll, i.e. one full trigger window later (config.go:22-23 MaxTriggerSeconds = 600).

unverified_low.title: DuressVisibilityHidden's doc names the raw alarm event topic as a duress sink; that topic never carries a duress event
unverified_low.claim: The exported doc comment states that `hidden` keeps duress "on the webhook and the raw alarm event topic only". The MQTT alarm plane has a closed set of six event types on <base>/alarm/<zone>/event (TRIGGER, SILENCED, FAILED_TO_ARM, DISARMED, ARMED, NOTIFICATION) and the publisher does not subscribe to AlarmDuressEvent at all, so no duress marker ever reaches that topic — a duress disarm is indistinguishable from an ordinary DISARMED. The engine's own comment states the opposite of the enum doc and is the correct one.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: An operator (or a maintainer choosing where to put the visibility gate) reads the enum contract and concludes that at `hidden` a duress use is still recoverable from the raw MQTT event plane, and therefore that a webhook is optional. It is not: with duress_visibility=hidden and no webhook, the event reaches no surface at all and the journal row is unreadable (see C8-alarm-3). The operator-facing i18n help text is accurate; only the code contract is wrong.
unverified_low.evidence: pkg/hmenum/security.go:270-273 `// DuressVisibilityHidden keeps duress on the webhook and the raw // alarm event topic only, reproducing the historical behaviour.` versus internal/north/mqtt/alarm_publisher.go:22-30 (the complete event-type set: alarmEventTypeTrigger/Silenced/FailedToArm/Disarmed/Armed/Notification — no duress) and :208-217 Start's subscription list (onStateChanged, onTriggered, onNotification, onJournalAppended, onReadinessChanged, onHealthChanged, onPanelChanged, onCodesChanged — no duress handler; `grep -rn "AlarmDuressEvent" internal/north/mqtt/` is empty). The correct statement is at internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:640-644: "The alarm MQTT publisher does NOT subscribe — a duress disarm therefore appears on the alarm plane as an ordinary disarm ... but also means that at visibility `hidden` an installation without a webhook is told nothing at all."

unverified_low.title: MaxPathsPerInvoke is advertised as 10 on two surfaces but never enforced on the invoke path
unverified_low.claim: The bridge advertises MaxPathsPerInvoke=10 both as BasicInformation attribute 0x0016 (basic_information.go:246-255 default, served at :589-590) and in the CASE SessionParameters TLV tag 7 (secure/sigma/sigma.go:489-490). Nothing enforces it. ValidateInvokeBatch (im/invoke.go:278-307) checks wildcard-in-batch, missing CommandRef, duplicate paths and duplicate CommandRefs, but has no count check, and dispatchInvokeRequest (bridge/receive_dispatch.go:376-428) adds none — it calls ValidateInvokeBatch and then dispatches every entry. matter.js rejects the whole action: InteractionServer.ts:950-955 `if (invokeRequests.length > this.#maxPathsPerInvoke) throw new StatusResponseError(..., Status.InvalidAction)`, evaluated before any command producer runs.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: A controller that packs more than 10 CommandDataIBs into one InvokeRequest has all of them executed (real device actuation on the CCU) instead of the action being rejected with InvalidAction. Because the InvokeResponse is assembled from every entry and shipped as a single datagram with no chunking, a large enough batch produces a body over udp.MaxDatagramSize and the send is refused (transport/udp/listener.go:243 `if len(payload) > MaxDatagramSize`), so the commands have already run but the controller receives nothing, reports the invoke as failed, and may retry — double-actuating the bridged devices.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/north/matter/cluster/core/basic_information.go:246-255 (`maxPaths = 10` with the matter.js DEFAULT_MAX_PATHS_PER_INVOKE citation), :589-590; internal/north/matter/secure/sigma/sigma.go:489-490 `if sp.MaxPathsPerInvoke != 0 { enc.putUint16(7, sp.MaxPathsPerInvoke) }`. internal/north/matter/im/invoke.go:278-307 (full ValidateInvokeBatch — `multiple := len(req.Invokes) > 1` is the only use of the length). internal/north/matter/bridge/receive_dispatch.go:396-412. Gold standard: ../matter.js/packages/node/src/node/server/InteractionServer.ts:950-955. internal/north/matter/transport/udp/listener.go:33 (MaxDatagramSize = 2048), :243.

unverified_low.title: chunkReportData cannot split a single oversized attribute report and emits it over budget; the cited MTU constant is refuted by the code
unverified_low.claim: addAttributeReport only starts a new chunk when the current chunk already holds something: `if len(body) > budget && (len(current.Reports) > 0 || len(current.EventReports) > 0)` (reply.go:329, mirrored for events at :348). When a single AttributeReport alone encodes larger than reportChunkPayloadBudget (1100, reply.go:288) the guard is false and the oversized candidate is accepted as-is at :338. The Matter list-element chunking matter.js/chip use for this case (AttributeReportIB carrying a ListIndex per element) does not exist on loom's report path. Separately, the constant's own doc comment (reply.go:280-281) asserts 'the IPv6 minimum MTU caps the wire datagram at 1280 bytes ([udp.MaxDatagramSize])' — udp.MaxDatagramSize is 2048 (transport/udp/listener.go:33), so the only hard backstop sits 768 bytes above the MTU the comment claims it is.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: Descriptor.PartsList on the root and aggregator endpoints is a single attribute holding every bridged endpoint id. Past roughly 350 bridged endpoints on one bridge its encoded report exceeds 1100 bytes, and the chunker ships one ReportData datagram larger than the 1280-byte IPv6 minimum MTU (IP fragmentation, which Matter controllers and border routers commonly drop); past ~2048 bytes the send is refused outright at listener.go:243 and the Subscribe-Initial or Read for that path never completes, so the controller never learns the bridge topology.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/north/matter/bridge/reply.go:322-340 (addAttributeReport) and :341-359 (addEventReport, identical guard); :288 `const reportChunkPayloadBudget = 1100`; :278-287 doc comment citing [udp.MaxDatagramSize] as 1280. internal/north/matter/transport/udp/listener.go:33 `const MaxDatagramSize = 2048`, :243 `if len(payload) > MaxDatagramSize`. PartsList is served from a live provider with no size bound: internal/north/matter/cluster/core/descriptor.go:128-135, wired at internal/north/matter/bridge/bridge.go:987-995 and :1029-1036.

unverified_low.title: resolveBridgeUniqueID treats a store read error as 'not persisted' and then overwrites the pinned UniqueID it exists to protect
unverified_low.claim: `if v, ok, err := store.GetSetting(ctx, matterstore.SettingUniqueID); err == nil && ok && v != ""` returns the pinned value only on a clean read. On a non-nil err (GetSetting wraps any non-ErrNoRows scan/query failure — internal/north/matter/store/settings.go:46-55) the function falls through, re-derives the UniqueID from the CURRENT mc.NodeLabel, and unconditionally SetSetting()s it, i.e. it overwrites the persisted quality-F value instead of failing or keeping the old one. This is the 'empty vs failed' shape: a failed read becomes an empty-but-successful result.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: An already-commissioned bridge whose node_label was changed after the UniqueID was first pinned reboots while the SQLite handle returns a transient error for the matter_settings SELECT (locked table, I/O error). The read error is swallowed, a new UniqueID is derived from the new node_label and written over the pinned one. UniqueID carries Matter §11.1.5.13 quality F, so every paired controller sees a different device identity and Apple/Google Home treat all bridged accessories as new — the exact failure the function was added to prevent.
unverified_low.evidence: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:1699-1712 (err is discarded, then `if err := store.SetSetting(ctx, matterstore.SettingUniqueID, uid); err != nil { logger.Warn(...) }`). internal/north/matter/store/settings.go:46-55 GetSetting returns ("", false, wrapped err) for any non-ErrNoRows failure. The doc at daemon_matter.go:1682-1688 states the value "is persisted on first sight and pinned across every later boot".

unverified_low.title: ExceptionToFailureReason's new Timeout bucket is unreachable for every south-bound transport error, because all three transports wrap deadline errors in ErrNoConnection, which is tested first

unverified_low.title: readEventFilterArray skips a non-struct container without draining it, desyncing the whole ReadRequest/SubscribeRequest decode

UnmarshalReadRequestTLV returns `im: invalid ReadRequest: EventRequests not array` and drops the entire request — including the valid filter and the FabricFiltered flag that followed it — instead of tolerating the unknown element per Matter forward-compat rules. unverified_low.title: north.matter.dev_rotate_unique_ids no longer rotates the root BasicInformation UniqueID, and a value salted while it was on stays pinned after it is turned off
unverified_low.claim: The wave moved the root UniqueID from a per-read derivation to a value persisted on first sight (matterstore.SettingUniqueID) and pinned through core.Config.UniqueID. DeriveUniqueID still mixes bootid.Salt(), but the salt is only consulted on the one boot that first writes the setting; every later boot short-circuits on the stored string. The DevRotateUniqueIDs knob therefore no longer affects endpoint 0 — and once a salted value has been stored, disabling the knob does not restore the deterministic unsalted value either.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: A developer enables north.matter.dev_rotate_unique_ids to force Apple Home to see an unambiguously new bridge after HMHome cache corruption (the documented purpose). Bridged endpoints rotate (endpoint/materialize.go:355), but the root node keeps the UniqueID stored on the first boot, so the root identity Apple caches never changes and the log line 'per-boot UniqueID salt active' overstates what happens. Symmetrically, a developer who ran one boot with the knob on and then turned it off keeps the random salted UniqueID for the life of the database.
unverified_low.evidence: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:1699-1711 resolveBridgeUniqueID returns the stored value first (`if v, ok, err := store.GetSetting(ctx, matterstore.SettingUniqueID); err == nil && ok && v != "" { return v }`) and only otherwise calls DeriveUniqueID + SetSetting. internal/north/matter/cluster/core/basic_information.go:639-644 DeriveUniqueID mixes bootid.Salt(); :652-657 uniqueID() returns pinnedUniqueID whenever non-empty. cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:199-208 enables rotation from mc.DevRotateUniqueIDs with the hint 'per-boot UniqueID salt active'. internal/north/matter/endpoint/materialize.go:354-355 (bridged endpoints) still derives per boot, so the knob is now half-effective rather than dead.

unverified_low.title: The custom-DP half of the un-ignore withdrawal cannot fire in the daemon; the test that justifies it uses the reverse of the pipeline's boot order
unverified_low.claim: ApplyUnIgnoredMarks now calls custom.SuppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints(dev) whenever any VALUES data point is not un-ignored (:251-283). In the real pipeline that pass has already run at device_pipeline.go:751, long before applyUnIgnoredMarks at :866, and it force-marks every VALUES/MASTER data point of a custom-DP device that has no forced usage. SetForcedUsage has no clearing counterpart, so by the time ApplyUnIgnoredMarks runs every candidate already satisfies `hasForcedUsage(dp)` and the re-run is a guaranteed no-op — on boot and on every runtime un-ignore reload (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_wiring.go:176, visibility_adapter.go:153, which call ApplyUnIgnoredMarks alone). The new test asserts the opposite order ('Boot order: the un-ignore mark first, then the custom-DP suppression pass'), which is the only order in which the guarded block can change anything, so the block is unverified by any test that reflects production. The observable outcome is still correct — the mark's withdrawal falls through to the NoCreate forced usage set at step 751 — so this is a dead branch plus a misleading pin, not a wrong result.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: Operator deletes an un_ignore pattern on a custom-DP device (e.g. HmIP-BROLL LEVEL_2). ApplyUnIgnoredMarks re-runs, ClearUnIgnored drops the mark, and the extra SuppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints walk executes but cannot change a single data point because every one already carries a forced usage. If the pipeline order is ever changed so the suppression pass runs before 751-equivalent marking, the regression this block is meant to catch would ship green, because the only test covering it constructs the inverted order itself.
unverified_low.evidence: internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:251 `withdrawn := false`, :266-268 `m.ClearUnIgnored(); reapplyValuesSuppression(...); withdrawn = true`, :271-283 `if withdrawn { custom.SuppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints(dev) }`. internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:751 `p.suppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints(interfaceID)` vs :866 `p.applyUnIgnoredMarks(interfaceID)` — 751 comes first. internal/model/custom/materialize.go:504-528 `if !deviceHasCustomDP(dev) { return }` ... `if hasForcedUsage(dp) { continue }` and :547-548 the pass covers ch.DataPoints() and ch.MasterDataPoints(). internal/model/datapoint/base.go:268-273 SetForcedUsage only ever sets. internal/store/visibility/operation_mode_test.go:541,564 TestApplyUnIgnoredMarksReHidesOnACustomDPDevice: `visibility.ApplyUnIgnoredMarks(dev, decider)` then `custom.SuppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints(dev)`. Checked and refuted as non-issues: reapplyValuesSuppression passing a nil decider matches production, since ApplyHiddenParameterMarksWithDecider (operation_mode.go:455-468) and ApplyInternalParameterMarksWithDecider (:380-392) both discard their decider and pass nil to markIfHidden/markIfInternal.

unverified_low.title: Central rows were narrowed for non-admins while two sibling viewer-open routes still hand out the CCU host, serial and callback ports
unverified_low.claim: maskCentralRow now blanks Host/Serial/Port/JSONRPCPort/Ports/Username/PasswordEnv/TLS for any identity below admin, and openapi documents the narrowing, on the stated ground that those fields tell an authenticated viewer where the CCU lives. Two sibling routes in the same authenticated group were not touched and still return exactly that: GET /api/v1/config returns ConfigSnapshot.Centrals[].Host plus the XML-RPC/BIN-RPC callback ports, and GET /api/v1/centrals/discovered returns Serial + Host for every CCU the discoverer has seen. unverified_low.title: Fleet /snapshot NDJSON stream shares the truncation bug the eventbus/tap fix explicitly targeted, but was left off the router's streaming exemption list
unverified_low.claim: router.go's streamingPaths (the fix for the verified rest_1 finding) exempts only /diagnostics/logs/stream and /diagnostics/eventbus/tap from the 30s router-wide deadline. GET .../snapshot?ndjson=1 (handlers.Snapshot, router.go:1283) uses the identical http.Flusher-per-line streaming pattern (writeSnapshotNDJSON, snapshot.go:247-289) but is not in streamingPaths, so it still runs under middleware.Timeout.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: A large multi-CCU fleet requests GET /api/v1/snapshot?ndjson=1&include=data_points over a slow/throttled connection (mobile, HA Ingress proxy). writeSnapshotNDJSON flushes one JSON line per interface/device/channel/data_point/room/function/program/sysvar; if the client can't drain the buffer fast enough for the whole fleet to flush inside the router's WriteTimeout (~30s, same default as the fixed tap/log routes), r.Context() is cancelled mid-stream, the write aborts silently, and the client receives a truncated NDJSON body with no error frame - the same failure mode rest_1 was written to fix, just on a third handler the fix's streamingPaths list didn't enumerate.
unverified_low.evidence: router.go:1365-1368 streamingPaths = {logs/stream, eventbus/tap} only; router.go:1283 pr.Get("/snapshot", handlers.Snapshot(...)) is registered under the same r.Use(timeoutExceptStreaming(d.WriteTimeout)) at router.go:599; snapshot.go:250-256 flusher.Flush() per emitted line, snapshot.go:117-119 wantsNDJSON(r) routes into it; snapshot.go has no local context.WithTimeout or http.ResponseController deadline override of its own.

unverified_low.title: New EditSessionRequest schema declares `token` required, contradicting its own description and the handler
unverified_low.claim: The schema added in this wave sets `required: [key, token]` while its own description two lines below says a request that omits `token` "is accepted syntactically", and both handlers only reject a missing `key` (422) — a missing `token` is accepted and answered 204/410.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: A client generated from the 6.1.0 spec (or any request validator) rejects `{"key":"channel:ABC:MASTER"}` client-side as invalid, although the daemon accepts it; conversely a spec-conformance test asserting the daemon rejects a token-less body fails against the real handler.
unverified_low.evidence: assets/openapi.yaml:12637-12646 (`required: [key, token]` + "a request that omits it is accepted syntactically"); internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:258-266 (CloseEditSession: only `if req.Key == ""` → 422, then `s.Close(req.Key, req.Token)` → 204) and :200-210 (HeartbeatEditSession: only `key` required).

reported_issues.scope: GitHub issue #579 (report, diagnostics dump, daemon ndjson log, both screenshots); consumer chain ../homematicip_local/custom_components/homematicip_local/{__init__.py,button.py,control_unit.py,generic_entity.py,tests/test_backup.py}; ../openccu-loom-client/openccu_loom_client/compat/aiohomematic/central/{__init__.py,adapter.py} and operations/backup.py; ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/central/coordinators/client.py for the backend that is NOT affected; openccu-loom origin/main internal/north/rest/router.go backup routes; homeassistant/components/button/__init__.py for ButtonEntity polling semantics.

findings.title: Backup button reads central.available before the loom central is started and never re-writes its state, so it is permanently unavailable on the loom backend
findings.claim: HmipLocalCreateBackupButton.available returns self._cu.central.available (button.py:272-274). For the openccu-loom backend that resolves to LoomCentralAdapter.available = self._state in (CentralState.Running, CentralState.Degraded) (../openccu-loom-client/openccu_loom_client/compat/aiohomematic/central/adapter.py:1125-1127). The adapter is constructed unstarted -- CentralConfig.create_central() docstring: 'Build the unstarted adapter. Call adapter.start() to connect' (central/__init__.py:111-112) -- with self._state = CentralState.Stopped (adapter.py:1016). _state is only ever assigned at four sites (adapter.py:1016 Stopped, 1187 Starting, 1239 Running, 1567 Stopped); Running is reached at the very END of start(). Home Assistant sets the platforms up BEFORE the central starts: __init__.py:218 'await hass.config_entries.async_forward_entry_setups(entry, HMIP_LOCAL_PLATFORMS)' then __init__.py:220 'await control.start_central()' -> control_unit.py:290 'await self._central.start()'. The button is added inside that forward (button.py:127 'async_add_entities([HmipLocalCreateBackupButton(control_unit=control_unit)])'), so its one and only state write happens while _state == Stopped -> available False. ButtonEntity carries _attr_should_poll = False (homeassistant/components/button/__init__.py:89) and the class has no async_added_to_hass, no subscription and no async_write_ha_state / async_schedule_update_ha_state call anywhere (button.py:256-296; the only state-write call sites in the integration are generic_entity.py:383/620, update.py:202/344, event.py:195, number.py:393, select.py:317 -- none of them this entity). The availability computed at add time is therefore frozen for the lifetime of the config entry.
findings.failure_scenario: Reporter's setup (loom backend, single central 'RM80-CM4-4GB', daemon 0.61.2 healthy): HA sets up the config entry -> button platform is forwarded -> HmipLocalCreateBackupButton is added while LoomCentralAdapter._state == Stopped -> HA writes state 'unavailable' -> start_central() then completes and _state becomes Running, but nothing re-writes the button's state. Result: 'Backup erstellen' shows 'nicht verfuegbar' forever, across HA restarts and entry reloads, while every other hub entity on the same device page (e.g. 'Anlernmodus HmIP-RF aktivieren', which uses self._data_point.available at generic_entity.py:523-525) is available -- exactly what the reporter's screenshot shows. Restarting the daemon or HA does not help. The native aiohomematic backend does not show the defect because ClientCoordinator.available is 'all(client.available for client in self._clients.values())' (../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/central/coordinators/client.py:123-125) over a dict that is still empty at platform-setup time (clients are only inserted during start, coordinators/client.py:383) -- all([]) is True, so the same button is written as available there. The defect is loom-specific and has existed since the loom backend shipped, which matches the reporter's empty 'last working version' field.
findings.evidence: ../homematicip_local/custom_components/homematicip_local/button.py:127 'async_add_entities([HmipLocalCreateBackupButton(control_unit=control_unit)])'; button.py:272-274 'def available(self) -> bool: ... return self._cu.central.available'; button.py:256-296 contains no state-write and no subscription. ../homematicip_local/custom_components/homematicip_local/__init__.py:218 'await hass.config_entries.async_forward_entry_setups(entry, HMIP_LOCAL_PLATFORMS)' / :220 'await control.start_central()'. ../homematicip_local/custom_components/homematicip_local/control_unit.py:290 'await self._central.start()'; control_unit.py:1477-1493 '...create_central()' returns the adapter. ../openccu-loom-client/openccu_loom_client/compat/aiohomematic/central/__init__.py:111-112 'async def create_central(...) -> LoomCentralAdapter: """Build the unstarted adapter. Call ``adapter.start()`` to connect."""'. ../openccu-loom-client/openccu_loom_client/compat/aiohomematic/central/adapter.py:1016 'self._state: CentralState = CentralState.Stopped'; adapter.py:1125-1127 'def available(self) -> bool: ... return self._state in (CentralState.Running, CentralState.Degraded)'; adapter.py:1239 'self._state = CentralState.Running' (last statement of start()). venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/homeassistant/components/button/__init__.py:89 '_attr_should_poll = False'. Contrast: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/central/coordinators/client.py:123-125 'return all(client.available for client in self._clients.values())' with coordinators/client.py:97 'self._clients: Final[dict[str, ClientProtocol]] = {}' and :383 'self._clients[client.interface_id] = client' inside client creation during start. Daemon side is healthy and exonerated: the reporter's log shows 'backup.storage.ready' dir=/usr/local/addons/openccu-loom/var/backups and 'wire.backup.restorer_ready' central=RM80-CM4-4GB, and origin/main internal/north/rest/router.go:1216-1228 registers POST/GET /backups and /backups/{id}/download.

findings.title: create_backup_and_download() returns the raw trigger dict, but the HA button reads .filename/.content off it — the press path would fail even once the entity is available
findings.claim: LoomCentralAdapter.create_backup_and_download() is typed and implemented as 'async def create_backup_and_download(self) -> dict[str, Any]: return await self._client.backup.trigger_backup()' (adapter.py:1586-1594), and BackupOperations.trigger_backup returns 'dict(payload or {})' from POST /backups (operations/backup.py:23-26) -- the trigger response, no archive bytes; its own docstring says the archive 'is fetched separately via client.backup.download_backup'. The consumer treats the return value as an object with .filename and .content: button.py:280-291 'backup_data = await self._cu.central.create_backup_and_download()' ... 'backup_path = backup_dir / backup_data.filename' ... 'backup_path.write_bytes(backup_data.content)'. A dict has neither attribute, so the press raises AttributeError, which is not a BaseHomematicException and is therefore not converted by the handler at button.py:295-296 -- HA surfaces an unhandled exception instead of a usable error. This was never caught because the tests hand the collaboration to itself: tests/test_backup.py:24-29 builds 'backup_data = MagicMock(); backup_data.filename = ...; backup_data.content = ...' and injects it via 'central.create_backup_and_download = AsyncMock(return_value=backup_data)' (e.g. tests/test_backup.py:133), so the real adapter's return shape is never exercised.
findings.failure_scenario: Once finding 1 is fixed and the entity becomes pressable, pressing 'Backup erstellen' against a loom daemon calls POST /backups, gets {id: ...} back, and then raises AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'filename'. No file is written to the backup directory and the operator gets an unhandled-exception traceback rather than 'Failed to create CCU backup: ...'. Fixing only the availability would turn a visibly dead button into a silently failing one.
findings.evidence: ../openccu-loom-client/openccu_loom_client/compat/aiohomematic/central/adapter.py:1586-1594 (signature '-> dict[str, Any]', body 'return await self._client.backup.trigger_backup()', docstring 'The downloadable archive is fetched separately via ``client.backup.download_backup`` once the daemon reports the backup id.'); ../openccu-loom-client/openccu_loom_client/operations/backup.py:23-26 'payload = await self._transport.request(method="POST", path="/backups", allow_retry=False); return dict(payload or {})' and :33-35 'async def download_backup(self, *, backup_id: str) -> bytes'. ../homematicip_local/custom_components/homematicip_local/button.py:280 / :286 / :291 / :295. ../homematicip_local/tests/test_backup.py:24-29 and :133 (MagicMock with .filename/.content injected as the return value).
